phrases.translation: All praise is for Allah Who created the heavens and the earth and made darkness and light.
phrases.explanation: The chapter opens by directing all praise and gratitude to Allah alone as the Creator of the heavens and the earth and the One who ordained night’s darkness and day’s light. By naming these foundational realities first, the verse grounds worship in creation itself. Everything by which human life subsists comes from Him without any partner assisting in bringing the world into being.

phrases.translation: Yet the disbelievers set up equals to their Lord ˹in worship˺
phrases.explanation: Despite living within Allah’s creation and depending on His provision, disbelievers treat created things or false deities as equals to their Lord in devotion. Early commentators discussed whether this criticism targets idolaters in particular, certain People of the Book, or every group that assigns partners or rivals to God. The wording itself rebukes anyone who equates another being with the sole Creator.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who created you from clay,
phrases.explanation: Human beings are reminded of their shared origin in clay through the creation of Adam, from whom humanity descended. Addressing all people through the substance of their first ancestor turns attention from cosmic creation in the previous verse to human existence itself. The One who formed living human beings from lifeless earth is alone worthy of exclusive worship.

phrases.translation: then appointed a term ˹for your death˺ and another known only to Him ˹for your resurrection˺
phrases.explanation: Human life runs between two divinely fixed limits. Most commentators explain the first term as the span from birth until death and the second, known only to Allah, as the appointed time of resurrection and the Hour, while another view relates the two terms to sleep and death. In either case, life, death, and return remain entirely under Allah’s decree.

phrases.translation: —yet you continue to doubt
phrases.explanation: After pointing to human creation from clay and the fixed terms governing life and resurrection, the verse rebukes persistent doubt about Allah’s power to resurrect and judge. If the Creator brought humanity into life from dust the first time, doubting His ability to restore them after death has no rational basis.

phrases.translation: He is the Only True God in the heavens and the earth.
phrases.explanation: Allah alone possesses true divinity across both the heavens and the earth, unlike idols or imagined partners that have no power in either realm. Affirming that He is God in both domains rules out any division of sovereignty between heaven and earth and reinforces why worship belongs exclusively to Him.

phrases.translation: He knows whatever you conceal and whatever you reveal, and knows whatever you do
phrases.explanation: Nothing in human life is hidden from Allah, whether kept secret within the heart or spoken and acted upon openly. He also knows everything people earn through their deeds, recording both obedience and disobedience so that each person will be justly repaid when returning to Him.

phrases.translation: Whenever a sign comes to them from their Lord, they turn away from it
phrases.explanation: Every time a clear proof, revelation, or indication of Allah’s oneness and the Prophet’s truthfulness reaches the deniers, they refuse to reflect on it or accept what it establishes. Their problem is not a lack of evidence from their Lord, but a habitual posture of turning away whenever guidance confronts them.

phrases.translation: They have indeed rejected the truth when it came to them,
phrases.explanation: The polytheists rejected the truth of the Quran and the prophethood of Muhammad as soon as it reached them, without pausing to reflect on its proofs. Their immediate dismissal stemmed from stubborn attachment to inherited idolatry rather than any defect in the revelation. Turning away from clear truth at first sight leaves a community responsible for the ruin that follows.

phrases.translation: so they will soon face the consequences of their ridicule
phrases.explanation: Because they mocked Allah’s revelation and treated its warnings of judgment as a joke, the very reality and punishment of what they used to ridicule will soon come to them in this world and in the hereafter. Mockery never delays the arrival of divine justice.

phrases.translation: Have they not seen how many ˹disbelieving˺ peoples We destroyed before them?
phrases.explanation: The deniers are urged to consider the many earlier generations destroyed before their time after rejecting Allah’s messengers. History itself stands as a warning that persistent denial is not without consequence, and that present communities are not immune to the moral laws that governed earlier peoples.

phrases.translation: We had made them more established in the land than you. We sent down abundant rain for them and made rivers flow at their feet.
phrases.explanation: Those earlier nations enjoyed greater worldly strength, firmer settlement, abundant rainfall, fertile crops, and flowing rivers than the Prophet’s immediate opponents in Mecca. They carved dwellings and prospered across the land by Allah’s leave, yet material prosperity and civic power were tests of gratitude rather than proof of divine approval or immunity from judgment.

phrases.translation: Then We destroyed them for their sins and replaced them with other peoples
phrases.explanation: When those prosperous communities met Allah’s favours with ingratitude, injustice, and rejection of His messengers, their wealth could not save them from destruction. Allah brought their era to an end because of their sins and raised other generations in their place as a warning to those who came after them.

phrases.translation: Had We sent down to you ˹O Prophet˺ a revelation in writing and they were to touch it with their own hands,
phrases.explanation: Even if Allah had sent down to the Prophet a physical Book written on parchment from heaven so that the Meccan polytheists could touch and feel the pages directly with their own hands, removing every sensory doubt, their hearts would still have resisted faith. Even the most direct physical spectacle cannot open eyes that have chosen disbelief in advance.

phrases.translation: the disbelievers would still have said, “This is nothing but pure magic!”
phrases.explanation: In their stubborn obstinacy, those who disbelieve would still have dismissed that tangible miracle by claiming that their eyes and hands had merely been bewitched by manifest sorcery. No physical spectacle can convince a heart determined to reject the truth. Calling undeniable miracles magic is the standard refuge of those who refuse to bow to revelation.

phrases.translation: They say, “Why has no ˹visible˺ angel come with him?”
phrases.explanation: The polytheists demanded that an angel appear visibly alongside the Prophet in its angelic form to testify that Allah had truly sent him. They objected to following a human messenger who lived among them, using this demand as an excuse to avoid accepting the revelation already before them.

phrases.translation: Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have certainly been settled ˹at once˺, and they would have never been given more time ˹to repent˺
phrases.explanation: Allah answers that if an angel had been sent down as demanded, their fate would have been sealed immediately without any further respite for repentance. Commentators explain this either as the immediate descent of annihilating punishment if they still disbelieved, as happened to earlier nations who demanded miracles, or as sight of the angel in its true form causing instant death or the arrival of the Hour.

phrases.translation: And if We had sent an angel, We would have certainly made it ˹assume the form of˺ a man
phrases.explanation: Because human beings in this life cannot bear beholding angels in their original created form, any angel sent to walk among people and deliver a message would have been placed in the form of a man. Sending an angel to address them directly would therefore still have presented them with a human form.

phrases.translation: —leaving them more confused than they already are
phrases.explanation: Seeing an angel in human form would have left the doubters in the very same confusion they already raised against a human prophet, since they would still have doubted whether the figure before them was really an angel or a man. Their own stubbornness and confusion would thus have returned upon them.

phrases.translation: ˹Other˺ messengers had already been ridiculed before you ˹O Prophet˺,
phrases.explanation: Consoling the Prophet over the jeers of the Meccan idolaters, Allah reminds him that many messengers before him were similarly mocked by their disbelieving peoples yet bore that abuse with patient steadfastness. Knowing that earlier prophets faced the same trial strengthens the believer’s resolve. Every messenger endured the scoffing of his contemporaries while waiting patiently for Allah’s decree.

phrases.translation: but those who mocked them were overtaken by what they used to ridicule
phrases.explanation: In the end, the mockers among those bygone nations were surrounded and engulfed by the very punishment they had laughed at and demanded in scorn. History proves that ridiculing divine warnings ends in inescapable ruin. What the arrogant treat as a joke in this world becomes the very reality that destroys them.

phrases.translation: Say, “Travel throughout the land and see the fate of the deniers.”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is instructed to tell his opponents to journey through the lands where earlier deniers once lived and reflect on the ruins they left behind. Observing how those communities ended in destruction and disgrace in this world, before the punishment of the hereafter, should serve as a sobering lesson.

phrases.translation: Ask ˹them, O Prophet˺, “To whom belongs everything in the heavens and the earth?” Say, “To Allah!”
phrases.explanation: The opponents are challenged with a foundational question about ownership and dominion over everything in the heavens and the earth, followed immediately by the only true answer: all of it belongs to Allah alone. Idols and alleged partners own nothing and cannot benefit or protect even themselves.

phrases.translation: He has taken upon Himself to be Merciful.
phrases.explanation: Although Allah owns and overpowers all creation, He has graciously bound Himself to mercy toward His servants. Rather than hastening punishment upon those who disobey or associate partners with Him, He grants them time, invites them to repent, and extends compassion across creation in this world and to the faithful in the hereafter.

phrases.translation: He will certainly gather ˹all of˺ you together for the Day of Judgment—about which there is no doubt.
phrases.explanation: Divine mercy in delaying punishment does not cancel final accountability. Allah solemnly swears that He will gather all people together for the Day of Resurrection, an event free of any real doubt, so that every person is repaid justly for what they did and those who persisted in denial face the reckoning they dismissed.

phrases.translation: But those who have ruined themselves will never believe
phrases.explanation: Those who wrong and ruin themselves by clinging to idolatry and rejecting Allah’s signs forfeit their own share of salvation. By trading guidance and lasting reward for rebellion, they remain unwilling to affirm Allah’s oneness, His promise and warning, and the truth of His Messenger.

phrases.translation: To Him belongs whatever exists in the day and night.
phrases.explanation: To Allah alone belongs every creature that rests or moves during the hours of the night and the day, all owned and governed under His sovereign dominion. Nothing in time or space lies outside the ownership of the Creator. Every creature that rests by night or moves by day depends at every moment on its Creator.

phrases.translation: And He is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: He is the All-Hearing who hears every word His creatures utter in secret or aloud, and the All-Knowing who knows every hidden intention and deed. Awareness of His constant hearing and knowledge calls every servant to reverent obedience. No secret whisper or hidden action escapes the One who hears all voices and knows all hearts.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Will I take any guardian other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, Who provides for all and is not in need of provision?”
phrases.explanation: In response to calls to venerate idols or seek their protection, the Prophet asks how anyone could take a guardian other than Allah, who originated the heavens and the earth without precedent. He sustains and feeds every creature while needing no sustenance or support from anything He created.

phrases.translation: Say, “I have been commanded to be the first to submit and not be one of the polytheists.”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet declares that his Lord commanded him to be the first among his people and era to submit wholeheartedly to Allah in obedience, and never to join those who associate partners with Him. True devotion requires complete surrender to the Creator rather than compromise with idolatry.

phrases.translation: Say, “I truly fear—if I were to disobey my Lord—the torment of a tremendous Day.”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet explains that he refuses every invitation to worship other than Allah because he fears the punishment of the tremendous Day of Resurrection if he were ever to disobey his Lord. Even the Messenger frames his steadfastness in terms of reverence and accountability before God.

phrases.translation: Whoever is spared the torment of that Day will have certainly been shown Allah’s mercy.
phrases.explanation: Whoever has Allah’s punishment turned away from him on the Day of Resurrection has truly been graced with the supreme mercy of his Lord. Deliverance from the Fire is the foundational gift of divine compassion. Safety from the punishment of the hereafter is the greatest gift a servant can ever receive.

phrases.translation: And that is the absolute triumph
phrases.explanation: Being spared the torment of Hell and admitted into Allah’s mercy in Paradise is the manifest, unmistakable triumph beside which every worldly success is insignificant. True victory is measured by a person’s final standing on Judgment Day. Every worldly gain fades beside the triumph of being spared the Fire on the Day of Judgment.

phrases.translation: If Allah touches you with harm, none can undo it except Him.
phrases.explanation: If Allah afflicts a person with poverty, illness, or hardship, neither carved idols nor any creature in the heavens or earth has the power to lift that affliction except Allah alone. Hardship exposes the utter helplessness of false gods. When affliction strikes, the powerlessness of every idol and false helper becomes unmistakably clear.

phrases.translation: And if He touches you with a blessing, He is Most Capable of everything
phrases.explanation: Conversely, if Allah grants you health, wealth, and ease, none can withhold His gift, for He has complete, irresistible power over all things including both trial and relief. Recognizing that harm and benefit rest solely in Allah’s hand requires worshipping Him alone. Because both relief from harm and bestowal of blessing belong solely to Allah, devotion belongs to Him alone.

phrases.translation: He reigns supreme over His creation. And He is the All-Wise, All-Aware
phrases.explanation: Allah is the irresistible Sovereign above all His servants, subduing every creature under His authority while none can overpower Him or escape His decree. In exercising that supreme dominion, He is All-Wise in everything He ordains and All-Aware of the hidden realities, benefits, harms, beginnings, and outcomes of all affairs.

phrases.translation: Ask ˹them, O Prophet˺, “Who is the best witness?” Say, “Allah is! He is a Witness between me and you.
phrases.explanation: When opponents demand testimony for the Prophet’s truthfulness, he is told to ask whose testimony is greatest and most beyond error or falsehood, then answer that Allah Himself is the supreme Witness between him and them, judging who speaks the truth and who rejects it.

phrases.translation: And this Quran has been revealed to me so that, with it, I may warn you and whoever it reaches.
phrases.explanation: The Quran was revealed to the Prophet so that he might warn the people of Mecca and every person across all nations and generations whom its message reaches. Early commentators emphasized that anyone whom the Quran reaches has received the Prophet’s warning and call to accountability before Allah.

phrases.translation: Do you ˹pagans˺ testify that there are other gods besides Allah?” ˹Then˺ say, “I will never testify ˹to this˺!”
phrases.explanation: The polytheists are confronted directly over their claim that other deities exist alongside Allah. Even if they insist on bearing witness to idols and false gods, the Prophet is commanded to declare unequivocally that he will never join them in testifying to such falsehood or acknowledging any rival to his Lord.

phrases.translation: ˹And˺ say, “There is only One God. And I totally reject whatever ˹idols˺ you associate with Him.”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet completes his testimony by affirming that God is only One, without partner or rival in worship, and by disavowing every idol or associate that people set up beside Him. Clear affirmation of divine oneness goes hand in hand with complete dissociation from polytheism.

phrases.translation: Those to whom We gave the Scripture recognize him ˹to be a true prophet˺ as they recognize their own children.
phrases.explanation: Those who received the earlier scriptures know from the descriptions preserved in their books that Muhammad is truly a prophet sent by Allah, or recognize the truth of this revelation, with a certainty comparable to recognizing their own children. Their familiarity with the signs leaves no excuse of ignorance.

phrases.translation: Those who have ruined themselves will never believe
phrases.explanation: Yet those who have brought ruin upon their own souls refuse to believe despite recognizing the truth. By suppressing what they know and rejecting the Messenger sent by Allah, they forfeit their share of lasting bliss in paradise and choose their own loss in the hereafter.

phrases.translation: Who does more wrong than those who fabricate lies against Allah or deny His signs?
phrases.explanation: No human being commits a greater wrong than the one who invents falsehood against Allah by attributing partners or false laws to Him, or who rejects the clear revelations and miracles Allah sends down. Both slandering Allah and denying His truth attack the very foundation of religion.

phrases.translation: Indeed, the wrongdoers will never succeed
phrases.explanation: Truly, those who wrong their own souls through such fabrication and denial will never attain salvation, safety, or lasting success in the hereafter. Falsehood can never lead its practitioners to a blessed end. Neither those who invent falsehood about Allah nor those who reject His truth can ever prosper.

phrases.translation: ˹Consider˺ the Day We will gather them all together
phrases.explanation: Remind them of the Day of Resurrection when Allah will gather all creation together on the plain of judgment, bringing both the polytheists and the beings they worshipped face to face. None will be able to hide or absent himself from that assembly. On that Day every worshipper will stand before Allah alongside whatever he used to invoke.

phrases.translation: then ask those who associated others ˹with Allah in worship˺, “Where are those gods you used to claim?”
phrases.explanation: Before all witnesses Allah will rebuke the idolaters by asking where the alleged partner-gods are whom they used to claim in the world could intercede for them or share in divinity. The question exposes the total absence of help from their idols. Demanding that they produce their alleged partners exposes the emptiness of their lifelong idolatry.

phrases.translation: Their only argument will be: “By Allah, our Lord! We were never polytheists.”
phrases.explanation: When put to the test on the Day of Judgment and asked about their false deities, their only reply or excuse will be to swear by Allah, their Lord, that they were never polytheists. Seeing that forgiveness and paradise belong to the people of monotheism, they will desperately attempt to deny their past idolatry.

phrases.translation: See how they will lie about themselves
phrases.explanation: Allah bids the Prophet to marvel at how the polytheists will lie against their own souls on Judgment Day by swearing they were never idolaters, hoping in vain that denial might spare them torment. Extreme terror on that Day will strip away their worldly bravado.

phrases.translation: and how those ˹gods˺ they fabricated will fail them
phrases.explanation: At the very moment they need help most, all the false deities and intercessors they invented in the world will vanish and abandon them completely. Everything worshipped beside Allah deserts its followers at the reckoning. False gods vanish precisely when their worshippers stand in the greatest need of help.

phrases.translation: There are some of them who ˹pretend to˺ listen to your recitation ˹of the Quran˺, but We have cast veils over their hearts—leaving them unable to comprehend it—and deafness in their ears.
phrases.explanation: Some of the Meccan disbelievers came to hear the Prophet recite the Quran, yet they listened only to the sound without open hearts or genuine reflection. Because of their persistent rejection, Allah placed coverings over their hearts and heaviness in their ears so that they did not grasp or benefit from its guidance.

phrases.translation: Even if they were to see every sign, they still would not believe in them.
phrases.explanation: Their resistance is so deeply rooted that even if every kind of sign and proof pointing to Allah’s oneness and the Prophet’s truth were shown to them, they would still refuse to believe. The obstacle lies in their closed disposition, not in the clarity of the signs.

phrases.translation: The disbelievers would ˹even˺ come to argue with you, saying, “This ˹Quran˺ is nothing but ancient fables!”
phrases.explanation: After witnessing clear proofs and hearing the Quran, they still come to dispute with the Prophet instead of accepting the truth, even arguing over rulings such as lawful slaughter and carrion. To justify their refusal, they dismiss the revelation as nothing more than written tales, chants, or fables passed down from ancient peoples.

phrases.translation: They turn others away from the Prophet and distance themselves as well.
phrases.explanation: Most commentators explain that the Meccan polytheists both prevented other people from listening to or following the Prophet and the Quran and kept themselves far away from him. Another early report applies the wording to Abu Talib protecting the Prophet from harm while remaining apart from his faith, though the surrounding passage directly describes the polytheists’ opposition.

phrases.translation: They ruin none but themselves, yet they fail to perceive it
phrases.explanation: By blocking people from Allah’s message and refusing to follow it themselves, they do not harm Allah or diminish the truth. Instead, they bring ruin only upon their own souls by earning divine wrath and punishment, even while remaining oblivious to the destruction they are preparing for themselves.

phrases.translation: If only you could see when they will be detained before the Fire!
phrases.explanation: If you were to behold the disbelievers when they are brought and held standing over the brink of Hellfire on Judgment Day, you would witness a scene of overwhelming terror and regret. Seeing the Fire with their own eyes shatters every illusion they held in life.

phrases.translation: They will cry, “Oh! If only we could be sent back, we would never deny the signs of our Lord and we would ˹surely˺ be of the believers.”
phrases.explanation: In anguish they will wish that they could be returned to the worldly life, promising that they would never again reject the signs of their Lord and would surely become true believers. Yet wishes spoken before the Fire cannot reopen the concluded test of earthly life.

phrases.translation: But no! ˹They only say this˺ because the truth they used to hide will become all too clear to them.
phrases.explanation: Their plea to return does not arise from genuine love of faith, but from terror when the evil deeds, disbelief, and truths they used to conceal or suppress in the world are laid bare before them on the Day of Resurrection and they face disgrace.

phrases.translation: Even if they were to be sent back, they would certainly revert to what they were forbidden. Indeed they are liars
phrases.explanation: Allah knows that if they were actually returned to worldly life and given another chance, they would go right back to the idolatry, denial, and disobedience forbidden to them. Their promise to believe if sent back is therefore exposed as a false claim driven only by fear of punishment.

phrases.translation: They insisted, “There is nothing beyond this worldly life and we will never be resurrected.”
phrases.explanation: In the world, the polytheists denied any life after death and insisted that existence ends with this present life without resurrection, reward, or punishment. Some commentators also note that if they were returned to the world, this is the very denial they would resume repeating.

phrases.translation: But if only you could see when they will be detained before their Lord! He will ask ˹them˺, “Is this ˹Hereafter˺ not the truth?” They will cry, “Absolutely, by our Lord!”
phrases.explanation: When those who denied resurrection are detained before their Lord’s judgment on the Day of Rising, they will be asked whether this resurrection and reckoning they used to reject is not the truth. Confronted with undeniable reality, they will swear by their Lord that it certainly is.

phrases.translation: He will say, “Then taste the punishment for your disbelief.”
phrases.explanation: Once they confess before their Lord that the resurrection is real after every excuse has vanished, confession can no longer spare them from judgment. They will be told to taste the painful punishment they used to deny and mock as the just consequence of their persistent disbelief throughout their worldly life.

phrases.translation: Losers indeed are those who deny the meeting with Allah until the Hour takes them by surprise, then they will cry, “Woe to us for having ignored this!”
phrases.explanation: Those who deny resurrection and the meeting with Allah make a ruinous bargain by trading paradise for the Fire. When the Hour overtakes them suddenly and they see what they forfeited, they will cry out in bitter remorse over having squandered their lives and neglected preparation for that Day.

phrases.translation: They will bear ˹the burden of˺ their sins on their backs. Evil indeed is their burden
phrases.explanation: They will come forth carrying the heavy load of their sins upon their backs, depicted in early commentary as their own evil deeds meeting them in foul and hideous form to ride them into the Fire. Evil indeed is the burden of guilt they chose to bear.

phrases.translation: This worldly life is no more than play and amusement,
phrases.explanation: The life of this world, when pursued apart from obedience to Allah, is nothing more than fleeting play and distracting amusement that quickly passes away and leaves its seeker empty-handed. Worldly glitter deceives only those who forget how soon it ends. Treating the temporary world as an end in itself blinds a person to the purpose of creation.

phrases.translation: but far better is the ˹eternal˺ Home of the Hereafter for those mindful ˹of Allah˺. Will you not then understand
phrases.explanation: By contrast, the everlasting abode of the hereafter is infinitely better for those who fear Allah and guard His limits, so people are urged to use their intellect to prefer the eternal over the temporary. Sound reason always chooses the lasting home of the hereafter over a fleeting distraction.

phrases.translation: We certainly know that what they say grieves you ˹O Prophet˺.
phrases.explanation: Allah consoles the Prophet by acknowledging the deep sorrow caused by his people’s accusations and stubborn rejection of the message he brought from his Lord. Knowing that Allah sees his grief, hears their insults, and stands with him strengthens the Messenger to remain patient despite their hostility.

phrases.translation: It is not your honesty they question—it is Allah’s signs that the wrongdoers deny
phrases.explanation: Many of the Prophet’s opponents knew his lifelong truthfulness and recognized inwardly that he was not a liar, as reflected in reports about Quraysh leaders admitting they did not doubt his personal honesty. Out of pride, tribal rivalry, and stubbornness, the wrongdoers were knowingly rejecting Allah’s signs and revelation.

phrases.translation: Indeed, messengers before you were rejected but patiently endured rejection and persecution until Our help came to them.
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is consoled with the reminder that messengers sent before him also faced stubborn rejection and painful persecution from their communities. Yet they bore that harm patiently without abandoning their mission or ceasing to call their people to Allah until divine help and deliverance arrived.

phrases.translation: And Allah’s promise ˹to help˺ is never broken. And you have already received some of the narratives of these messengers
phrases.explanation: No one can alter Allah’s words or break His promise to grant victory to His messengers over those who persist in opposing them. The accounts of earlier prophets already revealed to the Prophet show how Allah fulfilled His promise and encourage him to follow their patient example.

phrases.translation: If you find their denial unbearable, then build—if you can—a tunnel through the earth or stairs to the sky to bring them a ˹more compelling˺ sign.
phrases.explanation: Addressing the Prophet’s deep distress over his people’s turning away, the verse states that even if he could dig a passage into the earth or climb a ladder into heaven to bring them a sign beyond what Allah has already given, he could not force them to believe.

phrases.translation: Had Allah so willed, He could have guided them all. So do not be one of those ignorant ˹of this fact˺
phrases.explanation: If Allah had willed, He could have gathered all of them upon guidance through His grace and power. Knowing that faith and disbelief unfold under Allah’s prior knowledge and wise decree should keep the Prophet from grieving over their refusal as though he were unaware of this reality.

phrases.translation: Only the attentive will respond ˹to your call˺.
phrases.explanation: Only those who listen to the Quran with open, understanding hearts will answer the Prophet’s call and embrace faith. Hearing with the ears alone profits nothing unless the heart attends to the truth. True response to the prophetic call requires a living heart that listens with humility and care.

phrases.translation: As for the dead, Allah will raise them up, then to Him they will ˹all˺ be returned
phrases.explanation: As for the disbelievers whose hearts are spiritually dead to guidance, Allah will resurrect them from their graves on Judgment Day together with the physically dead, and to Him alone they will all return for reckoning. Those who remain spiritually dead in life will still be raised physically to face their Lord’s judgment.

phrases.translation: They ask, “Why has no ˹other˺ sign been sent down to him from his Lord?”
phrases.explanation: Stubbornly ignoring the miracle of the Quran, the Meccan polytheists asked why no sensory miracle of their own choosing had been sent down to Muhammad from his Lord. Demanding custom-made signs was their pretext for avoiding submission. They demanded new miracles not out of a desire to believe, but out of stubborn contention.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Allah certainly has the power to send down a sign”—though most of them do not know
phrases.explanation: Allah instructs the Prophet to reply that Allah is certainly able to send down any sign they demand, though most of them do not know that if such a sign came and they still disbelieved, immediate destruction would overtake them. Withholding a demanded sign is an act of mercy, since rejecting it after sight brings instant ruin.

phrases.translation: All living beings roaming the earth and winged birds soaring in the sky are communities like yourselves.
phrases.explanation: Every creature that walks or crawls upon the earth and every bird flying with its two wings forms distinct kinds and communities known, sustained, and governed by Allah just as human beings are. If Allah does not overlook animals and birds, He certainly does not overlook human actions.

phrases.translation: We have left nothing out of the Record. Then to their Lord they will be gathered all together
phrases.explanation: Nothing concerning these creatures, their provision, their lifespans, or their deeds is omitted from the preserved Record with Allah. Commentators explain their gathering to their Lord either as their being brought together through death, their resurrection on the Day of Judgment for justice to be settled among them, or both.

phrases.translation: Those who deny Our signs are ˹wilfully˺ deaf and dumb—lost in darkness.
phrases.explanation: Those who reject Allah’s revelations are spiritually deaf to hearing the truth and mute from speaking it, wandering in layers of darkness of disbelief where they cannot see the right way. Suppressing the faculties of truth leaves a person trapped in self-imposed gloom. Refusing to hear and speak the truth plunges the denier into layers of spiritual darkness.

phrases.translation: Allah leaves whoever He wills to stray and guides whoever He wills to the Straight Way
phrases.explanation: In His sovereign justice and grace, Allah leaves to stray whomever He wills among those who prefer blindness and places upon the straight path of Islam whomever He wills. Guidance to the straight path is Allah’s gracious gift to those who seek truth with open hearts.

phrases.translation: Ask ˹them, O Prophet˺, “Imagine if you were overwhelmed by Allah’s torment or the Hour
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is commanded to confront the polytheists by asking them to imagine what they would do if Allah’s devastating punishment in this world or the sudden terror of the Final Hour came upon them. Extreme crisis strips away every false pretence. Imagining the sudden arrival of divine punishment forces the conscience to drop its stubborn excuses.

phrases.translation: —would you call upon any other than Allah ˹for help˺? ˹Answer me˺ if your claims are true
phrases.explanation: In that moment of mortal peril, would they call upon their lifeless idols instead of Allah for rescue, if their claim that those idols possess divine power is true. Their own conscience knows that in real danger they turn only to Allah. In moments of real terror, even polytheists know that only the Creator can answer their cry.

phrases.translation: No! He is the only One you would call. And if He willed, He could remove the affliction that made you invoke Him.
phrases.explanation: Answering the question for them, Allah declares that in genuine distress they call upon Him alone, and if He wills in His mercy He removes the calamity regarding which they cried out to Him. Instinctive monotheism surfaces whenever human beings face mortal helplessness. Crisis strips away cultural habits of idolatry and reveals the soul’s innate dependence on Allah.

phrases.translation: Only then will you forget whatever you associate with Him ˹in worship˺.”
phrases.explanation: In that hour of terror they completely abandon and forget all the false deities and idols they used to associate with Allah during times of ease. Deities that are forgotten in crisis have no right to be worshipped in safety. Forgetting false gods during danger proves that they were never true partners with Allah at all.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We have sent messengers before you ˹O Prophet˺ to other people who We put through suffering and adversity ˹for their denial˺,
phrases.explanation: Allah reminds the Prophet that He sent messengers to many nations before him, and when those communities rejected His messengers He afflicted them with extreme poverty, famine, and bodily disease. Worldly hardship was sent as a wake-up call before final ruin. Hardships sent upon rebellious nations were merciful warnings meant to awaken them before final destruction.

phrases.translation: so perhaps they would be humbled
phrases.explanation: Allah tested them with those afflictions so that their arrogance might soften and they might humble themselves in sincere supplication and repentance before their Lord. Adversity fulfills its purpose only when it drives the heart back to Allah. Affliction serves its purpose when it breaks human pride and restores humble supplication to Allah.

phrases.translation: Why did they not humble themselves when We made them suffer?
phrases.explanation: Rebuking those bygone peoples, Allah asks why they did not humble themselves in repentance and prayer when His punishment and trial descended upon them. Refusing to bow even under affliction shows the utmost hardness of heart. When suffering fails to soften a community’s heart, its spiritual disease has reached a perilous stage.

phrases.translation: Instead, their hearts were hardened, and Satan made their misdeeds appealing to them
phrases.explanation: Rather than softening, their hearts grew hard like stone against faith, while Satan beautified the idolatry and sins they were committing so they persisted in them until they perished. Hardened hearts and Satan’s allurements work together to keep unrepentant sinners trapped in rebellion. When a heart refuses to soften under trial, Satan easily convinces it that evil is good.

phrases.translation: When they became oblivious to warnings, We showered them with everything they desired.
phrases.explanation: When they ignored the warnings brought by hardship and forgot the admonition they had been given, Allah opened upon them the gates of every worldly comfort, wealth, and health as a test of gradual drawing to ruin. Worldly abundance granted after warnings are ignored is a severe test rather than a sign of favour.

phrases.translation: But just as they became prideful of what they were given, We seized them by surprise, then they instantly fell into despair
phrases.explanation: At the very height of their exultation and pride over the worldly prosperity granted to them, Allah seized them suddenly with utter destruction, leaving them plunged into hopeless despair of every good. Sudden ruin at the peak of worldly pride leaves the heedless stripped of every hope.

phrases.translation: So the wrongdoers were utterly uprooted. And all praise is for Allah—Lord of all worlds
phrases.explanation: Thus the wrongdoing people who defied their Lord and denied His messengers were eradicated down to their last remnant. All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all worlds, for vindicating His messengers, fulfilling His promise to the faithful, and bringing just judgment upon persistent oppressors.

phrases.translation: Ask ˹them, O Prophet˺, “Imagine if Allah were to take away your hearing or sight, or seal your hearts—who else other than Allah could restore it?”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is instructed to ask the idolaters what deity other than Allah could ever restore their faculties if Allah took away their hearing, blinded their sight, and sealed their hearts from understanding. Since none besides Allah owns their senses, none besides Him deserves their worship.

phrases.translation: See ˹O Prophet˺ how We vary the signs, yet they still turn away
phrases.explanation: Allah bids the Prophet to observe how He sets forth His proofs and arguments in varied, clear ways so they may understand, yet the polytheists still turn away in stubborn refusal. Repeating proofs in varied forms leaves no excuse for those who stubbornly turn away.

phrases.translation: Ask, “Imagine if Allah’s punishment were to overwhelm you with or without warning
phrases.explanation: Ask the deniers to consider what will happen if Allah’s overwhelming punishment descends upon them suddenly by night without prior notice or openly by day after clear warning signs have appeared. Whether punishment arrives suddenly by night or openly by day, no rebel can ward it off.

phrases.translation: —who would be destroyed other than the wrongdoers?”
phrases.explanation: When that divine punishment arrives, none will be destroyed by it except the wrongdoers who wronged their own souls by worshipping idols and rejecting Allah’s messengers. Divine justice never destroys the innocent for the crimes of the wicked. Divine retribution targets those who wronged themselves through persistent idolatry and defiance.

phrases.translation: We have sent messengers only as deliverers of good news and as warners.
phrases.explanation: Allah clarifies that He sends His messengers solely as bearers of glad tidings of Paradise for those who obey Him and as warners of Hellfire for those who disobey Him, not to produce miracles on demand. Messengers are sent to convey glad tidings and clear warnings, while outcomes rest with Allah.

phrases.translation: Whoever believes and does good, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve
phrases.explanation: Whoever believes sincerely in the messengers and reforms his conduct through righteous deeds will have no fear of the terrors ahead in the hereafter, nor grieve over the worldly life he left behind. Sincere faith joined with righteous action secures complete safety from fear and sorrow in the hereafter.

phrases.translation: But those who deny Our signs will be afflicted with punishment for their rebelliousness
phrases.explanation: By contrast, those who reject Allah’s signs, oppose His commands, and deny the messengers sent to them will be struck directly by painful punishment. That torment afflicts them because of their persistent rebellion, falsehood, and refusal to remain within the bounds of obedience to their Lord.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I do not say to you that I possess Allah’s treasuries or know the unseen, nor do I claim to be an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me.”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is instructed to clarify his true station: he does not claim lordship over Allah’s treasuries, independent knowledge of the unseen, or angelic nature. Rather, he is a human messenger who strictly follows and conveys only the revelation sent down to him by Allah.

phrases.translation: Say, “Are those blind ˹to the truth˺ equal to those who can see? Will you not then reflect?”
phrases.explanation: He then asks whether the one who is blind to Allah’s proofs and guidance can ever be equal to the believer who sees the truth and walks by its light. This contrast calls listeners to reflect honestly on the evidence before them and abandon disbelief.

phrases.translation: Warn with this ˹Quran˺ those who are awed by the prospect of being gathered before their Lord
phrases.explanation: Allah commands the Prophet to warn by means of this Quran those whose hearts fear that they will be gathered before their Lord on the Day of Resurrection to answer for their deeds. Revelation benefits most those who already carry a sense of accountability. Those who dread standing before their Lord are the ones most receptive to the Quran’s warning.

phrases.translation: —when they will have no protector or intercessor besides Him—so perhaps they will be mindful ˹of Him˺
phrases.explanation: On that Day of gathering no soul will have any kinsman, patron, or idol besides Allah to protect it or intercede for it without His leave, a reminder given so that people may guard themselves through obedience. Knowing that no idol or patron can intercede without Allah’s leave inspires true mindfulness in life.

phrases.translation: ˹O Prophet!˺ Do not dismiss those ˹poor believers˺ who invoke their Lord morning and evening, seeking His pleasure.
phrases.explanation: When wealthy Quraysh leaders demanded that the Prophet send away poor and socially humble believers such as Bilal, Ammar, Suhayb, and Khabbab before they would sit with him, Allah forbade driving away those who sincerely worship and remember their Lord morning and evening seeking only His pleasure.

phrases.translation: You are not accountable for them whatsoever, nor are they accountable for you. So do not dismiss them, or you will be one of the wrongdoers
phrases.explanation: Neither the Prophet nor those poor believers bear the reckoning or responsibility for the provision and deeds of the other before Allah. Sending away sincere worshippers who seek Allah’s face merely to satisfy arrogant notables would put rejection in the wrong place and make one of the wrongdoers.

phrases.translation: In this way We have tested some by means of others, so those ˹disbelievers˺ may say, “Has Allah favoured these ˹poor believers˺ out of all of us?”
phrases.explanation: Allah tests the wealthy, arrogant nobles of Quraysh through the humble, poor believers who embraced Islam first, so that the proud chiefs ask in scorn whether Allah could really have favoured such lowly people with guidance ahead of them. Worldly elites often scorn the truth when they see the poor and humble embracing it ahead of them.

phrases.translation: Does Allah not best recognize the grateful
phrases.explanation: Refuting their worldly snobbery, Allah asks whether He does not know best who among His servants are truly grateful for His grace by opening their hearts to faith and obeying His Messenger. Allah measures people not by wealth or social rank, but by the gratitude and faith in their hearts.

phrases.translation: When the believers in Our revelations come to you, say, “Peace be upon you! Your Lord has taken upon Himself to be Merciful.
phrases.explanation: Whether addressing the poor believers whom Quraysh wanted driven away or repentant believers who came asking about past sins, the Prophet is instructed to welcome those who believe in Allah’s signs with the greeting of peace and the glad tidings that their Lord has bound Himself to mercy.

phrases.translation: Whoever among you commits evil ignorantly ˹or recklessly˺ then repents afterwards and mends their ways, then Allah is truly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
phrases.explanation: Anyone among the believers who commits a sin out of ignorance, since early commentators explain that every act of disobedience against Allah is committed in ignorance until a person turns back, and then repents afterward and reforms their conduct will find Allah All-Forgiving and Most Merciful.

phrases.translation: This is how We make Our signs clear,
phrases.explanation: Just as Allah has clarified the truth regarding the sincere believers and their arrogant detractors, so does He set forth His revelations and proofs in detail throughout the Quran. Clear guidance leaves no ambiguity between right and wrong. Detailed revelation illuminates the path of obedience so that no sincere seeker is left in doubt.

phrases.translation: so the way of the wicked may become distinct
phrases.explanation: By making the signs of truth unmistakably plain, the path of the wicked criminals who oppose Allah’s messengers becomes clearly exposed and distinguished from the path of the believers. Exposing the path of the wicked protects believers from being deceived by its outward prestige. Making the path of the wicked unmistakable protects the community from following their steps.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke besides Allah.”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is commanded to declare openly to the polytheists that his Lord has strictly forbidden him to worship any of the idols and false deities they call upon besides Allah. Clear dissociation from idolatry is the foundation of the prophetic call. The Prophet’s first duty is to renounce every object of worship invoked beside the Creator.

phrases.translation: Say, “I will not follow your desires, for I then would certainly be astray and not one of those ˹rightly˺ guided.”
phrases.explanation: He must further tell them that he will never follow their caprices and invented customs, because if he yielded to their desires he would go astray from the truth and cease to be among the rightly guided. Compromising revelation to please popular desires would mean abandoning guidance for manifest error.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Indeed, I stand on a clear proof from my Lord—yet you have denied it.
phrases.explanation: The Prophet declares to those who invite him back to idol worship that he stands upon a clear, unmistakable proof from his Lord regarding Allah’s oneness and the sincerity of worship due to Him alone, whereas his opponents have rejected both that proof and their Lord.

phrases.translation: That ˹torment˺ you seek to hasten is not within my power. It is only Allah Who decides ˹its time˺. He declares the truth. And He is the Best of Judges.”
phrases.explanation: When mockers challenge him to bring down immediate punishment or demanded miracles, the Prophet replies that sending torment is not in his hands. Judgment belongs solely to Allah, who either recounts the truth or decrees true judgment according to the two classical readings, and He is the Best of Judges.

phrases.translation: Say ˹also˺, “If what you seek to hasten were within my power, the matter between us would have already been settled.
phrases.explanation: When the mockers demanded that he bring down the threatened punishment at once, the Prophet was instructed to reply that if the torment they sought to hasten were in his own hands, he would have sent it down immediately to end the dispute between them.

phrases.translation: But Allah knows the wrongdoers best.”
phrases.explanation: Instead, the timing of punishment rests solely with Allah, who knows best the wrongdoers and the exact hour when their respite should end. Human impatience cannot hurry the wisdom of the All-Knowing Judge. Allah delays punishment according to His perfect knowledge of the wrongdoers and their appointed term.

phrases.translation: With Him are the keys of the unseen—no one knows them except Him. And He knows what is in the land and sea.
phrases.explanation: With Allah alone lie the keys and treasuries of the unseen, which no created being knows independently of Him. At the same time, He encompasses everything observable across the land and the sea, so both what is hidden from creatures and what is visible to them are fully known to Him.

phrases.translation: Not even a leaf falls without His knowledge, nor a grain in the darkness of the earth or anything—green or dry—but is ˹written˺ in a perfect Record
phrases.explanation: Not a single leaf drops in a forest, desert, or town without Allah knowing it, nor does a seed lie hidden in the dark layers of the earth, nor anything living and moist or withered and dry exist without being recorded in the Preserved Tablet.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who calls back your souls by night and knows what you do by day, then revives you daily to complete your appointed term.
phrases.explanation: Allah takes human souls back in sleep each night while knowing every deed and sin a person earns with their limbs during the day. He then awakens and restores them to consciousness each daytime so that each person completes the fixed lifespan decreed until death.

phrases.translation: To Him is your ˹ultimate˺ return, then He will inform you of what you used to do
phrases.explanation: Just as people are awakened each morning after sleep, their ultimate return after death is to Allah alone. On the Day of Resurrection He will inform them of everything they used to do in their worldly lives and repay each person justly for good or evil.

phrases.translation: He reigns supreme over all of His creation, and sends recording-angels, watching over you.
phrases.explanation: Allah holds supreme, irresistible authority above all His servants, in contrast to lowly idols that possess no power at all. He sends successive guardian angels who alternate by night and by day to watch over each person, preserving their deeds, provision, and appointed lifespan without letting anything be lost.

phrases.translation: When death comes to any of you, Our angels take their soul, never neglecting this duty
phrases.explanation: When the decreed moment of death arrives for any person and their appointed lifespan in this world reaches its end, the angels charged with taking souls receive their soul in full. Those angelic messengers carry out Allah’s command faithfully without falling short, delaying, or neglecting their duty.

phrases.translation: Then they are ˹all˺ returned to Allah—their True Master.
phrases.explanation: After the angels of death take their souls, all creatures are returned to Allah, their true Sovereign and Master who owns them in life and death alike. Death brings every soul back to its real Owner. Every soul returns at death to the true Master who created and governed it throughout life.

phrases.translation: Judgment is His ˹alone˺. And He is the Swiftest Reckoner
phrases.explanation: Unquestionably, the final judgment and decree belong exclusively to Allah without partner, and He is the swiftest of all reckoners, able to call the entire creation to account in a single moment. No delay or confusion can slow the reckoning of the One whose judgment encompasses all creation.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Who rescues you from the darkest times on land and at sea?
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is commanded to ask the polytheists who it is that rescues them from the terrifying darkness and perils of travel by land and stormy seas when every human means fails. Peril on land and sea reminds travelers that only the Creator commands the forces of nature.

phrases.translation: He ˹alone˺ you call upon with humility, openly and secretly: “If You rescue us from this, we will be ever grateful.”
phrases.explanation: In those moments of mortal danger they call upon Allah alone in humble, earnest pleading both aloud and in secret, promising that if He saves them from that peril they will surely be among the grateful. Earnest promises of gratitude made in danger bear witness against those who return to idolatry in safety.

phrases.translation: Say, “˹Only˺ Allah rescues you from this and any other distress,
phrases.explanation: Remind them that it is Allah alone, not any of their idols, who rescues them from the terrors of land and sea as well as from every other affliction and distress they face. Every deliverance from mortal distress comes solely from the mercy and power of Allah.

phrases.translation: yet you associate others with Him ˹in worship˺.”
phrases.explanation: Yet as soon as He delivers them safely to shore, they break their promise of gratitude and go right back to associating lifeless idols with Him in worship. Such ingratitude after rescue exposes the irrationality of polytheism. Returning to idol worship after being rescued by Allah alone is the height of ingratitude.

phrases.translation: Say, “He ˹alone˺ has the power to unleash upon you a torment from above or below you or split you into ˹conflicting˺ factions and make you taste the violence of one another.”
phrases.explanation: The One who rescues them also has full power to send punishment from above them, such as stones or flood from the sky, or from beneath their feet, such as the earth swallowing them up, or as another early view puts it, oppressive rulers above and unruly subordinates below, or to divide them into warring factions tasting one another’s violence.

phrases.translation: See how We vary the signs, so perhaps they will comprehend
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is invited to reflect with his heart on how Allah repeats and diversifies His proofs, warnings, and lessons among the polytheists in one form after another so that they might understand the danger of ingratitude and be restrained from persisting in idolatry and denial.

phrases.translation: Still your people ˹O Prophet˺ have rejected this ˹Quran˺, although it is the truth.
phrases.explanation: Despite the overwhelming proofs of Allah’s power and mercy, the Prophet’s own tribe of Quraysh denied the Quran and its warning of punishment, even though it is the undeniable truth from their Lord. Even the Prophet’s own kinsmen rejected the Quran despite knowing its truth and his honesty.

phrases.translation: Say, “I am not a keeper over you.”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is instructed to tell them that he has not been appointed as a guardian charged with compelling them to believe or protecting them from the consequences of their own choices, but only as a messenger to convey the truth. A messenger is charged with clear delivery of the truth, not with forcing unwilling hearts to believe.

phrases.translation: Every ˹destined˺ matter has a ˹set˺ time to transpire.
phrases.explanation: Every promised event and warning announced in revelation has a fixed time and appointed place when its truth will come to pass, whether in this world or on Judgment Day. Divine promises are never cancelled by delay. Every divine promise and threat moves steadily toward its appointed hour of fulfillment.

phrases.translation: And you will soon come to know
phrases.explanation: A stern warning assures the deniers that they will soon know with certainty the truth of what they were promised when death and punishment overtake them and regret no longer avails. When the decreed hour arrives, those who doubted will know the truth beyond any dispute.

phrases.translation: And when you come across those who ridicule Our revelations, do not sit with them unless they engage in a different topic.
phrases.explanation: Whenever the Prophet or the believers see people mocking, reviling, or engaging in vain ridicule of Allah’s revelations and signs, they are commanded to turn away and rise from that gathering rather than sitting with them until the speakers move on to another topic of conversation.

phrases.translation: Should Satan make you forget, then once you remember, do not ˹continue to˺ sit with the wrongdoing people
phrases.explanation: If Satan causes a believer to forget their Lord’s prohibition and remain seated while Allah’s signs are being ridiculed, they must rise and depart as soon as they remember, refusing to sit any longer with wrongdoing people who speak falsely and mockingly against Allah’s revelation.

phrases.translation: Those mindful ˹of Allah˺ will not be accountable for those ˹who ridicule it˺ whatsoever
phrases.explanation: As long as the believers avoid sitting in approval with those who mock Allah’s revelations, the God-fearing bear no share of guilt or accountability for the sins of the mockers. Each soul answers for its own conduct. Refusing to join the assemblies of mockery keeps believers clear of the mockers’ guilt.

phrases.translation: —their duty is to advise, so perhaps the ridiculers will abstain
phrases.explanation: However, the believers remain duty-bound to remind and admonish the mockers against trifling with Allah’s signs, so that they may fear Allah and desist from their ridicule. Patient admonition remains a duty in case reminders awaken fear of Allah in heedless hearts. Sincere counsel discharges the believer’s responsibility and offers the heedless a chance to reform.

phrases.translation: And leave those who take this faith ˹of Islam˺ as mere play and amusement and are deluded by ˹their˺ worldly life.
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told to turn away from those who treat religion as a subject for mockery and amusement because the fleeting adornments of worldly life have deceived them into forgetting their return to Allah. Early commentators note that this instruction to leave them was later followed by the revelation of fighting rulings.

phrases.translation: Yet remind them by this ˹Quran˺, so no one should be ruined for their misdeeds. They will have no protector or intercessor other than Allah. Even if they were to offer every ˹possible˺ ransom, none will be accepted from them.
phrases.explanation: Even so, he must continue reminding people with the Quran so that no soul is handed over to destruction and held hostage by its own sins on a Day when it will have neither protector nor intercessor besides Allah, and when no ransom of any size would ever be accepted.

phrases.translation: Those are the ones who will be ruined for their misdeeds. They will have a boiling drink and painful punishment for their disbelief
phrases.explanation: Those who persist in treating religion as play and amusement are the very ones delivered over to ruin and held in pledge for what their hands earned. When thirsty in hell, they will be given scalding water that cannot quench thirst, along with painful punishment for their disbelief.

phrases.translation: Ask ˹them, O Prophet˺, “Should we invoke, other than Allah, those ˹idols˺ which cannot benefit or harm us, and turn back to disbelief after Allah has guided us?
phrases.explanation: Answering polytheists who urged the Muslims to return to idol worship, the Prophet asks how anyone with sound reason could invoke lifeless wood or stone that can neither benefit nor harm, turning back on their heels into disbelief after Allah has guided them to Islam.

phrases.translation: ˹If we do so, we will be˺ like those disoriented by devils in the wilderness, while their companions call them to guidance, ˹saying˺, ‘Come to us!’
phrases.explanation: Turning back from faith to idolatry after guidance is likened to a traveller enticed by devils into a trackless wilderness where he wanders bewildered and lost, even while his companions on the right path call out to him to come back to guidance and safety.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Allah’s guidance is the ˹only˺ true guidance. And we are commanded to submit to the Lord of all worlds
phrases.explanation: Rejecting the idolaters’ claim that their ancestral religion was guidance, the Prophet declares that the path Allah has revealed and prescribed is the only true guidance, and that believers have been commanded to surrender themselves in sincere, exclusive obedience to the Lord of all worlds.

phrases.translation: establish prayer, and be mindful of Him. To Him you will all be gathered together
phrases.explanation: Along with submitting to the Lord of all worlds, believers are commanded to establish regular prayer and remain mindful of Allah by obeying His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, knowing with certainty that all people will be gathered back to Him on the Day of Resurrection.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who created the heavens and the earth in truth. On the Day ˹of Judgment˺ He will say, ‘Be!’ And there will be!
phrases.explanation: The Lord to whom believers submit is the One who created the heavens and the earth in truth, justice, and wisdom rather than in vain. On the Day of Resurrection when He says ‘Be’ to bring creation back to life, it comes into being at once by His command.

phrases.translation: His command is truth. All authority is His ˹alone˺ on the Day the Trumpet will be blown. He is the Knower of all—seen or unseen. And He is the All-Wise, All-Aware.”
phrases.explanation: His word and promise are absolute truth, and sole sovereignty belongs to Him on the Day when the Trumpet is blown to usher in the Resurrection. He knows both the unseen and the visible world, and He is All-Wise in His governance and All-Aware of all deeds.

phrases.translation: And ˹remember˺ when Abraham said to his father, Ȃzar, “Do you take idols as gods?
phrases.explanation: Recalling the model of pure monotheism whom the Arabs claimed to revere, Allah reminds the Prophet of when Abraham rebuked his father Azar for taking carved statues as gods to worship beside Allah. Abraham’s fearless question to his own father set the timeless example of rejecting ancestral idolatry.

phrases.translation: It is clear to me that you and your people are entirely misguided.”
phrases.explanation: Speaking with uncompromising clarity despite filial respect, Abraham declared that he saw both his father and their entire idolatrous nation wandering in manifest error far from the path of truth. True compassion for family and community requires telling them plainly when their worship has gone astray.

phrases.translation: We also showed Abraham the wonders of the heavens and the earth,
phrases.explanation: Just as Allah guided Abraham away from his people’s idols, He unveiled to his sight and insight the vast dominion and sovereign kingdom of the heavens and the earth, including the sun, moon, stars, and signs of creation. Contemplating the vast order of the heavens and earth reveals the single sovereign hand behind creation.

phrases.translation: so he would be sure in faith
phrases.explanation: Allah showed him that cosmic dominion so that Abraham would be among those who possess unshakeable certainty in Allah’s absolute oneness and have conclusive proof against the star- and idol-worshippers. Direct insight into the dominion of the universe gave Abraham unshakeable certainty and decisive proof.

phrases.translation: When the night grew dark upon him, he saw a star and said, “This is my Lord!”
phrases.explanation: Debating his people who worshipped celestial bodies, Abraham looked when night’s darkness covered him at a bright rising star and said by way of argument to test their claim, 'This is my Lord according to your view.' By starting from his people’s own astral beliefs, Abraham prepared to dismantle their error from within.

phrases.translation: But when it set, he said, “I do not love things that set.”
phrases.explanation: As soon as the star sank below the horizon and vanished, Abraham exposed its imperfection by declaring that he could never worship deities that set, disappear, and change from state to state, since the true Lord is ever-present. Anything that rises, sets, and vanishes is subject to change and cannot be the eternal Lord.

phrases.translation: Then when he saw the moon rising, he said, “This one is my Lord!”
phrases.explanation: Continuing his step-by-step refutation of astral worship, when Abraham saw the moon rising in fuller brightness across the night sky, he said to his people by way of argument, 'This one is my Lord.' Moving from the star to the brighter moon showed that greater brilliance still does not confer divinity.

phrases.translation: But when it disappeared, he said, “If my Lord does not guide me, I will certainly be one of the misguided people.”
phrases.explanation: When the moon too set and vanished from sight, Abraham pointed out to his people that unless his true Lord guided him to the truth, following such vanishing bodies would leave a person among the misguided. Without divine guidance, human beings easily mistake impressive created things for the Creator.

phrases.translation: Then when he saw the sun shining, he said, “This must be my Lord—it is the greatest!”
phrases.explanation: When morning broke and Abraham saw the sun rising in dazzling radiance, he said to his people in culminating argument, 'This is my Lord, for it is larger and brighter than the star and the moon.' Even the sun, the largest and brightest luminary in the sky, remains a servant bound by law.

phrases.translation: But again when it set, he declared, “O my people! I totally reject whatever you associate ˹with Allah in worship˺
phrases.explanation: Once the sun also set at the end of the day, proving it too was a subjugated creature, Abraham openly declared to his people that he was completely free of all the stars and idols they associated with Allah. When the sun too sank below the horizon, the case against worshipping celestial bodies was complete.

phrases.translation: I have turned my face towards the One Who has originated the heavens and the earth—being upright—
phrases.explanation: Having demonstrated that every setting celestial body is created, Abraham declared that he directed his worship and devotion exclusively to the One who originated the heavens and the earth without prior example, inclining purely to monotheism. True worship turns past every created object toward the Originator who brought the cosmos into being.

phrases.translation: and I am not one of the polytheists.”
phrases.explanation: He concluded his proclamation by affirming that he had no part with the polytheists who associate created stars, idols, or partners with their Creator in worship. Pure monotheism requires a clean break from every form of associating partners with Allah. True devotion to the Creator leaves no room in the heart for created partners.

phrases.translation: And his people argued with him. He responded, “Are you arguing with me about Allah, while He has guided me?
phrases.explanation: When Abraham’s people disputed with him in defense of their idols and claimed their deities were superior, he asked how they could argue with him about Allah’s sole divinity and exclusive right to worship after Allah had already granted him clear guidance, insight, and certainty.

phrases.translation: I am not afraid of whatever ˹idols˺ you associate with Him—˹none can harm me,˺ unless my Lord so wills. My Lord encompasses everything in ˹His˺ knowledge. Will you not be mindful
phrases.explanation: When they threatened that their gods would strike him with madness or harm for speaking against them, Abraham replied that lifeless idols cannot harm anyone and that nothing occurs except what his Lord wills. Since his Lord encompasses all things in knowledge, he urged them to reflect and take heed.

phrases.translation: And how should I fear your associate-gods, while you have no fear in associating ˹others˺ with Allah—a practice He has never authorized?
phrases.explanation: Abraham turns his people’s threat back against them, asking how he could fear helpless idols that can neither bring benefit nor even ward off his axe from themselves, while they feel no fear toward the Almighty Creator who sustains them when they associate partners with Him without any revealed proof or authority.

phrases.translation: Which side has more right to security? ˹Tell me˺ if you really know!”
phrases.explanation: He challenges them to judge honestly which of the two parties has a truer claim to safety from divine punishment in this world and the next: one who worships the single Almighty Lord sincerely, or those who worship powerless idols without any evidence from Allah.

phrases.translation: It is ˹only˺ those who are faithful and do not tarnish their faith with falsehood
phrases.explanation: Deciding the dispute over who truly deserves security, Allah declares that it belongs to those who believe in Him alone and do not mix or corrupt their faith with any injustice, explained by the Prophet himself as associating partners with Allah. Keeping faith pure of polytheism is the essential condition for safety on the Day of Judgment.

phrases.translation: who are guaranteed security and are ˹rightly˺ guided
phrases.explanation: To those pure monotheists alone belongs true safety from Allah’s punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and they are the ones rightly guided to the straight path in this world. Those who worship Allah alone enjoy both guidance in this life and lasting security in the hereafter.

phrases.translation: This was the argument We gave Abraham against his people.
phrases.explanation: That decisive proof demonstrating that whatever sets and changes cannot be God was the conclusive argument with which Allah inspired Abraham so that he overcame his idolatrous people. Prophetic argument prevails not by force, but by exposing the contradictions of falsehood through clear reason. Inspired reasoning dismantled centuries of astral superstition without needing a single sword.

phrases.translation: We elevate in rank whoever We please. Surely your Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: Through knowledge, wisdom, and prophetic proof Allah raises by many degrees whomever He wills among His servants, for the Lord is All-Wise in His governance and All-Knowing of who deserves elevation. Allah elevates His servants in rank through the wisdom and certainty He grants them.

phrases.translation: And We blessed him with Isaac and Jacob. We guided them all
phrases.explanation: In reward for Abraham’s steadfast monotheism when he left his people, Allah blessed him with his son Isaac and grandson Jacob, and guided every one of them to the straight path of prophethood and pure worship. Righteousness in one generation became a source of blessing for generations to follow.

phrases.translation: as We previously guided Noah and those among his descendants: David, Solomon, Job, Joseph, Moses, and Aaron. This is how We reward the good-doers
phrases.explanation: Allah guided them just as He had guided Noah before Abraham, and among the descendants of Noah and Abraham He guided David, Solomon, Job, Joseph, Moses, and Aaron, rewarding those who excelled in obedience with prophetic honour and lasting remembrance. Across generations and nations, all of Allah’s prophets shared the same reward for upright obedience.

phrases.translation: Likewise, ˹We guided˺ Zachariah, John, Jesus, and Elias, who were all of the righteous
phrases.explanation: From Noah’s wider descendants Allah likewise guided Zachariah, his son John, Jesus son of Mary, and Elias, whom commentators identify either as a prophet from Aaron’s priestly lineage or, in another early report, with Idris. All four were among the righteous who obeyed Allah and upheld His religion faithfully.

phrases.translation: ˹We also guided˺ Ishmael, Elisha, Jonah, and Lot, favouring each over other people ˹of their time˺
phrases.explanation: Continuing the line of guided prophets from Noah’s descendants, Allah names Abraham’s son Ishmael along with Elisha, Jonah, and Lot. Since Lot was Abraham’s nephew rather than his offspring, commentators note that the earlier pronoun of descent refers back to Noah, and each of these prophets was honoured with prophethood above the people of their age.

phrases.translation: And ˹We favoured˺ some of their forefathers, their descendants, and their brothers.
phrases.explanation: Along with those named prophets, Allah also favoured and guided many among their forefathers, their offspring, and their brethren in faith across the generations. Prophetic guidance formed a continuous chain uniting righteous ancestors and descendants. Divine favour passed along the prophetic lineage to unite fathers, children, and brethren in faith.

phrases.translation: We chose them and guided them to the Straight Path
phrases.explanation: Allah elected them for His service and directed them firmly to the straight path of Islam, the religion of pure monotheism free of any crookedness or idolatry. Divine election is accompanied by steadfast guidance upon the truth. Walking the straight path is the fruit of Allah’s choice and guiding grace.

phrases.translation: This is Allah’s guidance with which He guides whoever He wills of His servants.
phrases.explanation: The pure religion of monotheism upon which all those prophets walked is Allah’s own guidance, wherewith He directs whomever He wills among His servants through His grace. True guidance belongs to Allah alone to bestow. Every rightly guided servant owes his steadfastness to the guidance of his Lord.

phrases.translation: Had they associated others with Him ˹in worship˺, their ˹good˺ deeds would have been wasted
phrases.explanation: Yet so grave is the sin of polytheism that even if those noble prophets themselves had associated partners with Allah in worship, all the righteous deeds they had performed would have been completely nullified and lost. If prophets are not exempt from the ruin of shirk, no other person can ever excuse it.

phrases.translation: Those were the ones to whom We gave the Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood.
phrases.explanation: Those prophets from the line of Noah and Abraham were the ones upon whom Allah bestowed revealed scriptures such as the scrolls of Abraham and Moses, the Psalms, and the Gospel, along with sound understanding of divine rulings and wisdom and the honour of prophethood.

phrases.translation: But if these ˹pagans˺ disbelieve in this ˹message˺, then We have already entrusted it to a people who will never disbelieve in it
phrases.explanation: If the polytheists of Quraysh reject these revelations, Allah has already entrusted His message to a people who never disbelieve in it, identified by commentators either as those earlier prophets who upheld the truth, or as the Ansar and believers who embraced and defended Islam.

phrases.translation: These ˹prophets˺ were ˹rightly˺ guided by Allah, so follow their guidance.
phrases.explanation: Those eighteen prophets named before were rightly guided by Allah to His true religion, the observance of His limits, and steadfast obedience in trial, so the Prophet Muhammad is commanded to follow their path of pure monotheism and patient devotion rather than the ways of the idolaters.

phrases.translation: Say, “I ask no reward of you for this ˹Quran˺—it is a reminder to the whole world.”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is instructed to tell the polytheists of his people that he seeks no worldly payment, gift, or wage from them for conveying the Quran and calling them to guidance. His message is purely a reminder and warning for all peoples among humankind and jinn.

phrases.translation: And they have not shown Allah His proper reverence when they said, “Allah has revealed nothing to any human being.”
phrases.explanation: Those who denied revelation altogether failed to honour and revere Allah as He deserves when they claimed He had never sent down any scripture to a mortal. Commentators attribute this denial either to the Quraysh polytheists in their dispute with the Prophet or to certain Jewish polemicists who spoke in anger.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Who then revealed the Book brought forth by Moses as a light and guidance for people, which you split into separate sheets—revealing some and hiding much? You have been taught ˹through this Quran˺ what neither you nor your forefathers knew.”
phrases.explanation: They are refuted by pointing to the Torah brought by Moses as a light and guidance, which was copied onto separate parchment sheets with some parts shown and much concealed, such as prophecies of Muhammad, while through revelation believers were taught knowledge neither they nor their forefathers previously knew.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Allah ˹revealed it˺!” Then leave them to amuse themselves with falsehood
