phrases.explanation: Because the deniers cannot deny that Allah revealed the Book of Moses, the Prophet is told to proclaim that Allah alone sent it down as light and guidance, and then leave the obstinate mockers to plunge and toy about in their idle falsehood until Allah’s judgment overtakes them.

phrases.translation: This is a blessed Book which We have revealed—confirming what came before it—so you may warn the Mother of Cities and everyone around it.
phrases.explanation: Just as Allah revealed the Torah to Moses, He has sent down this Quran as a blessed Book rich in benefit, confirming the earlier scriptures in calling to monotheism, so that the Prophet may warn the Mother of Cities, Mecca, and all peoples across the earth around it.

phrases.translation: Those who believe in the Hereafter ˹truly˺ believe in it and guard their prayers
phrases.explanation: Whoever truly believes in the hereafter, the resurrection, and the final reckoning affirms the truth of this revealed Book because they hope for Allah’s reward and fear His punishment, unlike deniers of the return to Allah, and they carefully guard their prescribed prayers in their proper times and limits.

phrases.translation: Who does more wrong than the one who fabricates lies against Allah or claims, “I have received revelations!”—although nothing was revealed to them—or the one who says, “I can reveal the like of Allah’s revelations!”?
phrases.explanation: No one commits a graver wrong than someone who invents lies about Allah by falsely claiming prophethood when nothing was revealed to him, or who boasts that he can produce the like of Allah’s revelation. Commentators link these descriptions to false claimants such as Musaylima and al-Aswad al-Ansi, and to Abdullah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh when he apostatized before later repenting.

phrases.translation: If you ˹O Prophet˺ could only see the wrongdoers in the throes of death while the angels are stretching out their hands ˹saying˺, “Give up your souls! Today you will be rewarded with the torment of disgrace for telling lies about Allah and for being arrogant towards His revelations!”
phrases.explanation: If the Prophet could behold such wrongdoers in the agonies of death as the angels stretch forth their hands to strike them and demand their souls, he would witness a terrifying sight. They are told that this day they will suffer humiliating punishment for lying against Allah and arrogantly scorning His verses.

phrases.translation: ˹Today˺ you have come back to Us all alone as We created you the first time—leaving behind everything We have provided you with.
phrases.explanation: On the Day of Resurrection Allah will rebuke the idolaters because they return to Him singly and alone, barefoot and stripped of wealth, children, and followers, just as He created them the first time, having left behind their backs everything He once granted them in the world.

phrases.translation: We do not see your intercessors with you—those you claimed were Allah’s partners ˹in worship˺. All your ties have been broken and all your claims have let you down.”
phrases.explanation: They are asked in rebuke why the false gods they claimed were partners of Allah and intercessors for them are nowhere to be seen beside them. Every worldly bond of kinship, friendship, and status has been severed, and all the intercession they falsely claimed has vanished from them.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah is the One Who causes seeds and fruit stones to sprout. He brings forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living.
phrases.explanation: Turning to the proofs of Allah’s sole lordship in creation, the verse reminds people that Allah alone cleaves open the dry grain to bring forth green crops and splits the date-stone to bring forth the palm tree. He brings the living plant or creature out of what is lifeless and brings the lifeless seed or drop out of the living.

phrases.translation: That is Allah! How can you then be deluded ˹from the truth˺
phrases.explanation: The One who performs all these wondrous acts of splitting the grain and date-stone and bringing life out of death is Allah alone, so how can rational people be turned away from worshipping their Creator and Sustainer to serve lifeless idols that neither hear nor see and can neither harm nor benefit?

phrases.translation: He causes the dawn to break, and has made the night for rest and ˹made˺ the sun and the moon ˹to travel˺ with precision.
phrases.explanation: Demonstrating His power over time and light, Allah cleaves the darkness of night with the break of dawn, appoints the night as a tranquil time of rest for His creatures, and sets the sun and moon moving in exact, calculated courses. Every daily cycle of rest and reckoning depends on His design.

phrases.translation: That is the design of the Almighty, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: That flawless cosmic order is the measured decree of the Almighty, whom nothing can resist in His sovereignty, and the All-Knowing, whose knowledge encompasses the movement and benefit of every created thing. Precision in nature points directly to the wisdom and power of its Maker.

phrases.translation: And He is the One Who has made the stars as your guide through the darkness of land and sea.
phrases.explanation: Allah is the One who created the stars in the night sky so that travelers may be guided by their positions through the deep darkness of desert tracks on land and trackless waters at sea. Celestial bodies exist to serve human navigation, not to be worshipped as gods.

phrases.translation: We have already made the signs clear for people who know
phrases.explanation: Thus Allah has explained His proofs and signs in creation in full clarity for a people who possess knowledge and reflect on how every creature serves the wisdom of the Creator. Those who know recognize the difference between the sign and the Lord who made it.

phrases.translation: And He is the One Who originated you all from a single soul, then assigned you a place to live and another to ˹be laid to˺ rest.
phrases.explanation: Allah alone brought all humanity into being from a single soul, Adam, and appointed for each person a place of settlement and a temporary repository, explained by early commentators as the father’s loins and the mother’s womb or as the earth in life and the grave at death. Every stage of human existence is planned by Allah.

phrases.translation: We have already made the signs clear for people who comprehend
phrases.explanation: Allah has set forth these unmistakable proofs of His creative power in detail for a people who understand His reminders and grasp the lessons embedded in their own origin and mortality. Reflecting on where we came from and where we rest awakens humility before our Maker.

phrases.translation: And He is the One Who sends down rain from the sky—causing all kinds of plants to grow—producing green stalks from which We bring forth clustered grain.
phrases.explanation: Allah alone sends down rain from the sky, bringing forth every kind of vegetation by which humans, livestock, beasts of burden, and birds are nourished and grow, and producing fresh green shoots from which ears of grain such as wheat and barley grow clustered one upon another.

phrases.translation: And from palm trees come clusters of dates hanging within reach. ˹There are˺ also gardens of grapevines, olives, and pomegranates, similar ˹in shape˺ but dissimilar ˹in taste˺.
phrases.explanation: From the spathes of date-palms come heavy clusters of dates hanging low within easy reach of those who gather them, alongside gardens of grapevines, olives, and pomegranates whose leaves and outward forms resemble one another while their fruits differ markedly in taste, sweetness, and quality.

phrases.translation: Look at their fruit as it yields and ripens! Indeed, in these are signs for people who believe
phrases.explanation: People are invited to observe the fruit when it first emerges in small unripe form and then as it ripens and matures into something sweet and wholesome to eat. Reflecting on these changing stages proves the governance of the One Creator for people who believe in Allah.

phrases.translation: Yet they associate the jinn with Allah ˹in worship˺, even though He created them, and they falsely attribute to Him sons and daughters out of ignorance.
phrases.explanation: Despite all these proofs of Allah’s sole creative power, the polytheists set up the jinn and devils as partners with Allah by obeying them in idol worship even though Allah created them, and out of sheer ignorance they falsely fabricate sons and daughters for Allah. Both obeying devils and inventing offspring for God slander the Creator.

phrases.translation: Glorified and Exalted is He above what they claim
phrases.explanation: Glorified, pure, and exalted is Allah far above having any partner, rival, son, or daughter as the ignorant polytheists falsely attribute to Him. Transcendent perfection belongs to the One who created all beings without need of any companion. Nothing in creation shares the majesty of the One who brought all things into being.

phrases.translation: ˹He is˺ the Originator of the heavens and earth. How could He have children when He has no mate?
phrases.explanation: Allah is the Originator who brought the heavens and the earth into existence without any prior model, so how could He possibly have a child when He has no consort or mate, since offspring arise only between two compatible mates. Absolute uniqueness makes the claim of divine offspring impossible.

phrases.translation: He created all things and has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of everything
phrases.explanation: Rather than begetting anything, Allah created every existing thing from nothing by His command, and He possesses complete, all-encompassing knowledge of all that He has created. Universal creation and omniscience leave no room for partners or children. He who created everything and knows everything has no need of offspring or helpers.

phrases.translation: That is Allah—your Lord! There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. ˹He is˺ the Creator of all things, so worship Him ˹alone˺.
phrases.explanation: The One possessing these attributes of originating the cosmos and knowing all things is Allah, your true Lord, besides whom no deity deserves worship. since He is the Creator of everything, humanity is commanded to worship Him alone without partner. Exclusive creation requires exclusive devotion.

phrases.translation: And He is the Maintainer of everything
phrases.explanation: Moreover, Allah is the Guardian, sustainer, and disposer over every existing thing, preserving His creatures and managing their provision and affairs at every moment. The One who sustains all creation is the only worthy object of trust. Entrusting every affair to the Maintainer of all things frees the heart from fear of creatures.

phrases.translation: No vision can encompass Him, but He encompasses all vision. For He is the Most Subtle, All-Aware
phrases.explanation: Human sight cannot encompass Allah in His majesty, even though, as early authorities explain, believers in Paradise will be honoured with seeing their Lord without their vision ever encompassing His boundless greatness, whereas He encompasses all sight. He is the Most Subtle in power and perception, the All-Aware of every created thing.

phrases.translation: Indeed, there have come to you insights from your Lord. So whoever chooses to see, it is for their own good. But whoever chooses to be blind, it is to their own loss.
phrases.explanation: Unmistakable proofs and inner insights have come to humanity from their Lord through the Quran. whoever sees the truth by them and believes benefits his own soul, while whoever blinds himself to them harms only himself. Revelation places the moral choice squarely before each individual.

phrases.translation: And I am not a keeper over you
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is commanded to tell them that he is not a guardian watching over their deeds to compel their faith, but only a messenger charged with delivering Allah’s clear proofs. Each person bears the consequence of whether he opens or shuts his eyes to the truth.

phrases.translation: And so We vary our signs to the extent that they will say, “You have studied ˹previous scriptures˺,”
phrases.explanation: Thus Allah varies His proofs, parables, and warnings in the Quran so that the deniers, astonished by its depth yet unwilling to believe, claim that Muhammad studied and learned these accounts from the People of the Book. Even their false accusation inadvertently acknowledged the rich knowledge contained in the revelation.

phrases.translation: and We make this ˹Quran˺ clear for people who know
phrases.explanation: While the stubborn dismiss it as borrowed learning, Allah makes the Quran’s signs and truths unmistakably clear for a people who possess genuine knowledge and recognize divine speech. Receptive minds find illumination in the very verses over which sceptics stumble. The very versatility of Quranic proof illuminates the knowledgeable while confounding the stubborn.

phrases.translation: ˹O Prophet!˺ Follow what is revealed to you from your Lord—there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him—
phrases.explanation: Allah commands His Messenger to follow steadfastly and act upon the Quran revealed to him from his Lord, affirming that there is no deity worthy of worship except Him alone. Steadfast adherence to revelation is the prophet’s anchor amidst opposition. Following revealed truth without compromise is the core of prophetic servitude.

phrases.translation: and turn away from the polytheists
phrases.explanation: At the same time he is instructed to turn away patiently from the abuse and foolish demands of the idolaters, an instruction revealed before the later command to fight those who waged war against the believers. Patient disregard of pagan provocation kept the mission focused on conveying truth.

phrases.translation: Had Allah willed, they would not have been polytheists.
phrases.explanation: Consoling the Prophet over their persistent disbelief, Allah states that had He willed to compel their hearts, none of them would have associated partners with Him in worship. Yet divine wisdom decreed that faith in this world should be a test of moral choice. Human freedom to accept or reject guidance is part of the wise test of earthly life.

phrases.translation: We have not appointed you as their keeper, nor are you their maintainer
phrases.explanation: Allah has neither appointed the Prophet as a guardian responsible for guarding them from sin nor made him a trustee charged with managing their livelihood and affairs. Relieved of responsibility for their stubbornness, the Messenger need only deliver the message faithfully. Knowing that guidance belongs to Allah relieves the Messenger of grief over stubborn deniers.

phrases.translation: ˹O believers!˺ Do not insult what they invoke besides Allah or they will insult Allah spitefully out of ignorance.
phrases.explanation: When the polytheists of Quraysh warned that they would revile Allah unless the Muslims stopped insulting their idols, Allah forbade the Prophet and the believers from cursing those false deities lest that give ignorant idolaters an occasion to revile Allah out of spite, enmity, and transgression without knowledge.

phrases.translation: This is how We have made each people’s deeds appealing to them. Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them of what they used to do
phrases.explanation: Just as idol worship seemed attractive to the polytheists, Allah has allowed every community’s chosen conduct, whether obedience or disobedience, to appear pleasing to them in this world. Ultimately all will return to their Lord, who will inform them of what they used to do and repay them accordingly.

phrases.translation: They swear by Allah their most solemn oaths that if a sign were to come to them, they would certainly believe in it.
phrases.explanation: The polytheists of Quraysh swore their most solemn, binding, and emphatic oaths by Allah that if the Prophet brought them a miraculous physical sign like those given to earlier communities, they would certainly believe in his prophethood and affirm that what he brought came truly from Allah.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Signs are only with Allah.” What will make you ˹believers˺ realize that even if a sign were to come to them, they still would not believe
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told to reply that miracles lie solely with Allah, who sends them as He wills. Addressing the believers who hoped that a demanded sign might win Quraysh over, Allah asks what makes them realize that even if it came, those stubborn deniers still would not believe.

phrases.translation: We turn their hearts and eyes away ˹from the truth˺ as they refused to believe at first,
phrases.explanation: Because they willfully rejected the Quran the very first time it came to them, Allah turns their hearts and eyes away from accepting the truth even if every demanded miracle were shown to them. Persisting in initial denial brings the punishment of spiritual blindness. Deliberate rejection of truth when it first arrives hardens the heart against all later proofs.

phrases.translation: leaving them to wander blindly in their defiance
phrases.explanation: Allah leaves them wandering in confusion and perplexity within their own insolent rebellion, unable to find the straight path they repeatedly scorned. Those who choose defiance over clear truth are left to stumble in their own error. Spiritual confusion is the inevitable result of choosing arrogance over clear revelation.

phrases.translation: Even if We had sent them the angels, made the dead speak to them, and assembled before their own eyes every sign ˹they demanded˺, they still would not have believed
phrases.explanation: Even if Allah had granted every extreme demand of the polytheists by sending angels down before their eyes, raising the dead from their graves to testify to Muhammad’s truth, and gathering every miracle face to face before them, they still would not have believed. Even the most overwhelming sensory miracles cannot force faith into a heart determined to deny.

phrases.translation: —unless Allah so willed. But most of them are ignorant ˹of this˺
phrases.explanation: None of them can believe unless Allah wills to guide their hearts to faith, yet most of the disbelievers are ignorant that guidance rests in Allah’s hand rather than in the mere display of miracles. Miracles alone never produce faith without divine grace. Faith is born when Allah opens the heart, not merely when the eye beholds wonders.

phrases.translation: And so We have made for every prophet enemies—devilish humans and jinn—whispering to one another with elegant words of deception.
phrases.explanation: Consoling the Prophet over his people’s hostility and urging him to patience, Allah explains that He has tested every prophet before him with rebellious enemies from among humans and jinn who whisper adorned, deceptive speech to one another in order to delude people and turn them away from the truth.

phrases.translation: Had it been your Lord’s Will, they would not have done such a thing. So leave them and their deceit
phrases.explanation: Had Allah willed to restrain them or compel their faith, they would never have carried out their hostility and deception. Since Allah tests His servants through such opposition, the Prophet is told to leave them and the falsehoods they fabricate until Allah’s judgment overtakes them.

phrases.translation: so that the hearts of those who disbelieve in the Hereafter may be receptive to it,
phrases.explanation: Allah permits human and jinn devils to whisper gilded, deceptive speech so that the hearts of those who deny the resurrection and reckoning of the hereafter incline toward that falsehood. Denial of final accountability leaves the heart vulnerable to every glittering deception. Forgetting the hereafter makes embellished falsehood sound attractive to heedless ears.

phrases.translation: be pleased with it, and be persistent in their evil pursuits
phrases.explanation: Once their hearts incline to Satan’s gilded whispers, they become well-pleased with falsehood and continue earning the evil deeds and sins that lead them to ruin. Choosing to delight in deception seals their persistence in wrongdoing. Delighting in Satan’s whispers leads directly to persistence in sinful action.

phrases.translation: ˹Say, O Prophet,˺ “Should I seek a judge other than Allah while He is the One Who has revealed for you the Book ˹with the truth˺ perfectly explained?”
phrases.explanation: Responding to idolaters who urged compromise over their gods, the Prophet asks how he could seek any judge other than Allah to decide between truth and falsehood when there is no judge more just than Allah, who has sent down the Quran with every ruling and proof set forth in detail.

phrases.translation: Those who were given the Scripture know that it has been revealed ˹to you˺ from your Lord in truth. So do not be one of those who doubt
phrases.explanation: Even if the polytheists of Quraysh deny the Quran, the learned people of the Torah and the Gospel recognize from their own scriptures that this Book has been sent down from the Lord in truth to distinguish truth from falsehood, so neither the Prophet nor the believers should ever entertain doubt.

phrases.translation: The Word of your Lord has been perfected in truth and justice.
phrases.explanation: The Word of your Lord in the Quran is complete and perfected in absolute truth regarding all that it reports and promises, and in perfect justice regarding all that it commands and forbids. Neither falsehood nor unfairness can ever enter divine revelation. Every report from Allah is true and every command from Him is just.

phrases.translation: None can change His Words. And He is the All-Hearing, All- Knowing
phrases.explanation: No creature can alter, annul, or falsify Allah’s Words and decrees, and He is the All-Hearing of what people say and the All-Knowing of what they do. Unchanging divine truth stands above every human attempt at distortion. Human schemes can never alter what the All-Hearing, All-Knowing Lord has decreed.

phrases.translation: ˹O Prophet!˺ If you were to obey most of those on earth, they would lead you away from Allah’s Way.
phrases.explanation: Allah warns the Prophet that if he were to follow the majority of people on earth, who at that time were steeped in polytheism and invented taboos, they would lead him astray from Allah’s straight religion. Truth is known by divine proof rather than by counting the crowd.

phrases.translation: They follow nothing but assumptions and do nothing but lie
phrases.explanation: For those majorities follow nothing in their idol worship and dietary taboos except baseless conjecture inherited from their fathers, and they do nothing but fabricate lies against Allah based on guesswork. Conjecture can never take the place of revealed certainty. Following popular guesswork instead of revelation leads only to falsehood and ruin.

phrases.translation: Indeed, your Lord knows best who has strayed from His Way and who is ˹rightly˺ guided
phrases.explanation: The Prophet’s Lord knows better than all creation which of His creatures strays from His path by following devilish whispers and which of them remains steadfast upon true guidance, so the Prophet and the believers must hold fast to Allah’s command rather than popular custom.

phrases.translation: So eat only of what is slaughtered in Allah’s Name if you truly believe in His revelations
phrases.explanation: Believers are commanded to eat of the lawful livestock over which Allah’s Name has been pronounced in proper slaughter by monotheists according to His revealed religion, rather than carrion or animals sacrificed to idols, and to reject the deceptive arguments of idolaters, if they truly believe in Allah’s signs.

phrases.translation: Why should you not eat of what is slaughtered in Allah’s Name when He has already explained to you what He has forbidden to you—except when compelled by necessity?
phrases.explanation: Nothing should prevent believers from eating meat lawfully slaughtered in Allah’s Name when He has already spelled out in detail what is forbidden to them, such as carrion and animals dedicated to idols, while excusing even those prohibitions when someone is driven by dire necessity.

phrases.translation: Many ˹deviants˺ certainly mislead others by their whims out of ignorance. Surely your Lord knows the transgressors best
phrases.explanation: Many among the polytheists lead people astray, or go astray themselves according to the two canonical readings, by declaring things lawful or unlawful out of ignorant personal whim without any proof from Allah, and the Lord knows best who transgresses His bounds and oversteps His limits.

phrases.translation: Shun all sin—open and secret. Indeed, those who commit sin will be punished for what they earn
phrases.explanation: People are commanded to abandon every form of sin, both outward and inward, which commentators explain either as public and private acts of disobedience generally, or specifically as open and clandestine sexual immorality. Those who earn such sins will surely be repaid for what they committed.

phrases.translation: Do not eat of what is not slaughtered in Allah’s Name. For that would certainly be ˹an act of˺ disobedience.
phrases.explanation: Believers are forbidden to eat carrion that died without lawful slaughter or animals sacrificed in the name of idols rather than Allah, for consuming such meat in defiance of Allah’s command is grave disobedience, whereas meat lawfully slaughtered by monotheists and the People of the Book remains permissible.

phrases.translation: Surely the devils whisper to their ˹human˺ associates to argue with you. If you were to obey them, then you ˹too˺ would be polytheists
phrases.explanation: The devils whisper specious arguments to their human allies among the idolaters so that they dispute with the believers by asking why they eat what they slaughter themselves yet refuse carrion that died by Allah’s decree. If believers obeyed them by treating carrion as lawful against Allah’s prohibition, they too would become polytheists.

phrases.translation: Can those who had been dead, to whom We gave life and a light with which they can walk among people, be compared to those in complete darkness from which they can never emerge?
phrases.explanation: One who was spiritually dead in disbelief until Allah gave him life through faith and a guiding light by which he walks uprightly among people cannot be compared to an obstinate disbeliever trapped in layers of darkness from which he never emerges. Early reports apply this contrast to believers such as Hamza or Umar and stubborn enemies such as Abu Jahl.

phrases.translation: That is how the misdeeds of the disbelievers have been made appealing to them
phrases.explanation: Just as Abu Jahl and his fellow idolaters were left wandering in the darkness of error while disputing with the believers over forbidden foods, the evil deeds and false arguments of the disbelievers have been made appealing to their eyes so that they persist in disobedience.

phrases.translation: And so We have placed in every society the most wicked to conspire in it.
phrases.explanation: Just as the chiefs of Mecca plotted against the Prophet in his city, so has Allah allowed the leading criminals and arrogant notables in every town to plot and scheme within it to bar people from faith. Opposition from corrupt elites is a recurring test in history.

phrases.translation: Yet they plot only against themselves, but they fail to perceive it
phrases.explanation: In reality their evil schemes rebound solely against their own souls by earning them destruction in this world and torment in the hereafter, though in their heedlessness they do not perceive it. Every plot against Allah’s truth ultimately ruins the plotter. Those who scheme against divine truth are in reality digging their own spiritual grave.

phrases.translation: Whenever a sign comes to them, they say, “We will never believe until we receive what Allah’s messengers received.”
phrases.explanation: When a clear proof of the Prophet’s truth comes to the arrogant leaders of Quraysh, they declare out of envy and pride that they will never believe in him or his rulings unless they themselves are given revelation and miracles directly, just as Allah’s messengers were given.

phrases.translation: Allah knows best where to place His message. The wicked will soon be overwhelmed by humiliation from Allah and a severe punishment for their evil plots
phrases.explanation: Allah answers that He alone knows best where to place His prophetic message and whom to choose as His messenger, since that choice belongs to the Sender rather than to those sent to. Those criminals who scheme against His religion will soon suffer humiliation before Allah and severe torment.

phrases.translation: Whoever Allah wills to guide, He opens their heart to Islam. But whoever He wills to leave astray, He makes their chest tight and constricted as if they were climbing up into the sky.
phrases.explanation: When Allah wills to guide a servant, He casts light into their heart so that their chest expands joyfully to receive Islam. When He wills to leave someone astray, He makes their chest tight and constricted against faith, so that accepting monotheism feels as unbearable as trying to climb up into the sky.

phrases.translation: This is how Allah dooms those who disbelieve
phrases.explanation: Just as Allah constricts the chest of the stubborn denier until faith cannot enter it, He places defilement, which early commentators explain as Satanic mastery, impurity in which there is no good, and divine punishment, upon those who refuse to believe in Him and His Messenger.

phrases.translation: That is your Lord’s Path—perfectly straight. We have already made the signs clear to those who are mindful
phrases.explanation: This religion of Islam and its rulings set forth in the Quran is the Lord’s path, perfectly straight and free of crookedness, which believers must hold fast to in what it permits and forbids. Allah has explained His signs in detail for people of understanding who remember and take heed.

phrases.translation: They will have the Home of Peace with their Lord,
phrases.explanation: For those whose hearts Allah opens to Islam and who walk the straight path, there awaits in the hereafter the Home of Peace, Paradise, where they are safe from every sorrow, death, and harm, in the presence of their Lord. The Home of Peace rewards believers with eternal safety in the company of their Lord.

phrases.translation: Who will be their Guardian because of what they used to do
phrases.explanation: Allah Himself will be their Protector, Helper, and Friend as a generous reward for the righteous deeds of obedience they used to perform during their worldly lives. Divine friendship and eternal peace crown a life of faithful service. Righteous action in this brief life earns the everlasting guardianship of Allah.

phrases.translation: ˹Consider˺ the Day He will gather them ˹all˺ together and say, “O assembly of jinn! You misled humans in great numbers.” And their human associates will say, “Our Lord! We benefited from each other’s company, but now we have reached the term which You appointed for us.”
phrases.explanation: On the Day when Allah gathers the rebellious devils and their human followers together, He will rebuke the jinn for having misled vast numbers of humankind. Their human allies will confess that each side took worldly advantage of the other, as humans obeyed the devils’ promptings while the devils enjoyed their compliance, until death and the appointed Resurrection arrived.

phrases.translation: ˹Then˺ He will say, “The Fire is your home, yours to stay in forever, except whoever Allah wills to spare.” Surely your Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: Allah will decree that the Fire of hell is their permanent abode in which they will remain forever, except for whatever period Allah wills to except in His sovereign knowledge, such as the interval between resurrection and entering hell. Truly the Lord is All-Wise in His governance and All-Knowing of His creatures’ end.

phrases.translation: This is how We make the wrongdoers ˹destructive˺ allies of one another because of their misdeeds
phrases.explanation: Just as rebellious jinn and idolatrous humans were joined together in mutual delusion, Allah makes wrongdoers allies of one another in disbelief, gives some of them power over others in the world, and joins them together in the Fire because of the sins they used to earn.

phrases.translation: ˹Allah will ask,˺ “O assembly of jinn and humans! Did messengers not come from among you, proclaiming My revelations and warning you of the coming of this Day of yours?”
phrases.explanation: On the Day of Resurrection Allah will rebuke the disbelievers of jinn and humankind by asking whether messengers from among them, human prophets and jinn warners who conveyed the prophets’ call as commentators explain, did not come reciting His revelations and warning them of meeting this Day.

phrases.translation: They will say, “We confess against ourselves!” For they have been deluded by ˹their˺ worldly life. And they will testify against themselves that they were disbelievers
phrases.explanation: With every excuse cut off on the Day of Resurrection, they will confess against themselves that the messengers did bring the warning, though the fleeting allure and leadership of worldly life deluded them into arrogance, and they will bear witness against their own souls that they lived and died as disbelievers.

phrases.translation: This ˹sending of the messengers˺ is because your Lord would never destroy a society for their wrongdoing
phrases.explanation: Allah sends messengers to warn jinn and humans and establish conclusive proof against them because your Lord would never destroy towns unjustly for their polytheism and sins before warning them first. Divine justice never punishes before the truth has been conveyed. Sending messengers establishes clear proof so that no town is ever destroyed unjustly.

phrases.translation: while its people are unaware ˹of the truth˺
phrases.explanation: No community is seized with destruction while its inhabitants remain unwarned and unaware of Allah’s commands through the arrival of messengers. Sending prophets removes every excuse of ignorance before judgment falls. Accountability before Allah begins only after the message of truth has been made known.

phrases.translation: They will each be assigned ranks according to their deeds.
phrases.explanation: On the Day of Resurrection every worker among the obedient and the disobedient will be assigned distinct ranks and levels in Paradise or in Hell corresponding to the deeds they performed. Eternal stations reflect the moral quality of earthly actions. Every person’s rank in the hereafter corresponds precisely to the deeds he earned in life.

phrases.translation: And your Lord is not unaware of what they do
phrases.explanation: Your Lord is never heedless of anything that His servants do of good or evil, but records every action with complete knowledge to requite it in full. Perfect divine awareness guarantees that no deed goes unrewarded or unjudged. Nothing done in secret or in public escapes the awareness of the Sovereign Judge.

phrases.translation: Your Lord is the Self-Sufficient, Full of Mercy.
phrases.explanation: Your Lord is completely Self-Sufficient, needing nothing from His creatures or their worship, while at the same time He is the Possessor of vast mercy toward His servants. His commands are given entirely for human benefit rather than any need of His own. Because Allah needs nothing from creation, every command He gives is an act of mercy.

phrases.translation: If He wills, He can do away with you and replace you with whoever He wills, just as He produced you from the offspring of other people
phrases.explanation: If you disobey Him, He has the power to remove and destroy you altogether and bring after you whatever other obedient people He wills as successors, just as He originally brought you into being from the descendants of earlier nations. No generation is indispensable before the Creator who can replace the rebellious at will.

phrases.translation: Indeed, what you have been promised will certainly come to pass. And you will have no escape
phrases.explanation: The polytheists are warned that the reckoning, resurrection, and punishment promised to them by their Lord for persisting in disbelief will certainly arrive without fail, and they will never be able to outrun, escape, or frustrate Allah’s power anywhere on earth, for they remain entirely within His grasp.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O my people! Persist in your ways, for I ˹too˺ will persist in mine.
phrases.explanation: Warning his stubborn tribe, the Prophet is commanded to tell them to continue acting according to their chosen way of idolatry if they insist, while he continues acting steadily according to the way of obedience Allah commanded him. When opponents refuse every reminder, steady perseverance on the truth is the believer’s answer.

phrases.translation: You will soon know who will fare best in the end. Indeed, the wrongdoers will never succeed.”
phrases.explanation: They will soon know with certainty to whom the blessed final outcome of victory in this world and Paradise in the hereafter will belong, for the wrongdoers who worship idols will never succeed. The final outcome of history and judgment always vindicates the righteous against the wrongdoers.

phrases.translation: The pagans set aside for Allah a share of the crops and cattle He created, saying, “This ˹portion˺ is for Allah,” so they claim, “and this ˹one˺ for our associate-gods.”
phrases.explanation: Exposing the arbitrary superstitions of pre-Islamic polytheism, Allah recounts how the idolaters set aside a portion of the crops and livestock that He alone created and assigned it to Him, while designating another portion of that very provision for their idols and false associate-gods according to their baseless claim.

phrases.translation: Yet the portion of their associate-gods is not shared with Allah while Allah’s portion is shared with their associate-gods. What unfair judgment
phrases.explanation: Whenever anything from the share assigned to Allah spilled over or fell short in the idols’ share, they gave it to their idols, proclaiming that Allah had no need, yet if anything from the idols’ share mixed into Allah’s share, they returned it to the idols. Evil indeed was their unjust judgment.

phrases.translation: Likewise, the pagans’ evil associates have made it appealing to them to kill their own children—only leading to their destruction as well as confusion in their faith.
phrases.explanation: Just as devils and temple custodians enticed the polytheists to divide their crops and livestock for idols, those evil associates made the killing and live burial of their children for fear of poverty or shame seem virtuous to them, in order to bring about their ruin and obscure the religion of Abraham for them.

phrases.translation: Had it been Allah’s Will, they would not have done such a thing. So leave them and their falsehood
phrases.explanation: Had Allah willed to guide them to the truth and restrain them from that crime, they would not have killed their children or invented such practices in obedience to devils. The Prophet is therefore told to leave them and the lies they fabricate against Allah until His punishment overtakes them.

phrases.translation: They say, “These cattle and crops are reserved—none may eat them except those we permit,” so they claim.
phrases.explanation: Out of their own invention, the polytheists declared certain dedicated cattle and crops taboo and off-limits without any permission from Allah, claiming falsely that no one was allowed to eat from them except those whom they permitted, such as male temple attendants while excluding women.

phrases.translation: Some other cattle are exempted from labour and others are not slaughtered in Allah’s Name—falsely attributing lies to Him. He will repay them for their lies
phrases.explanation: They also declared the backs of certain camels, such as the bahira, sa'iba, and ham, forbidden to ride or burden, and dedicated other cattle over which they refused to mention Allah’s Name when riding, milking, or performing pilgrimage, falsely attributing all these taboos to Allah, who will repay them for their slander.

phrases.translation: They ˹also˺ say, “The offspring of this cattle is reserved for our males and forbidden to our females; but if it is stillborn, they may all share it.”
phrases.explanation: Concerning what was in the bellies of those dedicated cattle, interpreted by early commentators as their unborn young or their milk, the idolaters decreed that if a calf was born alive it belonged exclusively to their men and was forbidden to their women, whereas if it was stillborn both men and women shared in eating it.

phrases.translation: He will repay them for their falsehood. Surely He is All-Wise, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: Allah will repay them with the punishment they deserve for the false rulings and lies they described with their tongues in forbidding what He did not forbid and attributing that slander to Him. Truly He is All-Wise in governing His creation and All-Knowing of their fabrications.

phrases.translation: Lost indeed are those who have murdered their own children foolishly out of ignorance and have forbidden what Allah has provided for them—falsely attributing lies to Allah.
phrases.explanation: Utterly ruined in both worlds are the pre-Islamic polytheists who buried their infant daughters alive out of foolishness and ignorance, and who declared unlawful the livestock and crops Allah had provided for them while falsely attributing those taboos to Allah. Invented religion drove them both to murder their own children and to slander Allah’s law.

phrases.translation: They have certainly strayed and are not ˹rightly˺ guided
phrases.explanation: By combining the murder of their own children with fabricated religious prohibitions against Allah, they strayed far from the path of truth and were never among the rightly guided. Cruelty and superstition are the inevitable fruits of abandoning revelation. Forsaking revelation plunges society into moral cruelty and religious delusion.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who produces gardens—both cultivated and wild—and palm trees, crops of different flavours, olives, and pomegranates—similar ˹in shape˺, but dissimilar ˹in taste˺.
phrases.explanation: Reminding people that He alone created the provisions they arbitrarily declared unlawful, Allah states that He brought forth trellised orchards such as supported grapevines and untrellised gardens growing along the ground or in the wild, along with date-palms, crops of varied flavours, and olives and pomegranates similar in foliage yet different in taste.

phrases.translation: Eat of the fruit they bear and pay the dues at harvest, but do not waste. Surely He does not like the wasteful
phrases.explanation: Believers are commanded to eat of these fruits when they ripen and to give the obligatory due from their produce on the day of harvest, while avoiding extravagance, whether by squandering wealth beyond bounds or withholding what is due, for Allah does not love the wasteful.

phrases.translation: Some cattle are fit for labour, others are too small.
phrases.explanation: Among the livestock Allah created for human benefit are large camels and cattle strong enough to carry heavy loads in travel, and smaller sheep and goats close to the ground that yield wool, milk, and meat. Every class of livestock serves a distinct human need.

phrases.translation: Eat of what Allah has provided for you and do not follow Satan’s footsteps. Certainly, he is your sworn enemy
phrases.explanation: People are therefore commanded to eat gratefully of the lawful livestock and crops Allah has provided and never follow the footsteps of Satan by forbidding what Allah made lawful, since Satan is a manifest enemy to humanity. Inventing prohibitions against Allah’s lawful gifts is one of Satan’s oldest traps for humanity.

phrases.translation: ˹Allah has created˺ four pairs: a pair of sheep and a pair of goats—
phrases.explanation: Beginning the detailed refutation of pagan livestock taboos, Allah names eight mates of grazing livestock starting with four here: two of sheep, male and female, and two of goats, male and female. Specifying each pair exposes the incoherence of their invented restrictions. Enumerating the pairs of livestock one by one leaves pagan superstition nowhere to hide.

phrases.translation: ask ˹them, O Prophet˺, “Has He forbidden ˹to you˺ the two males or the two females or what is in the wombs of the two females? Tell me with knowledge, if what you say is true.”—
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is commanded to ask the polytheists in biting irony whether Allah forbade the two males, or the two females, or the unborn offspring in the wombs of the females, challenging them to produce real knowledge for their claims if they are truthful. Demanding real knowledge exposes how their taboos rested on arbitrary whim rather than revelation.

phrases.translation: and a pair of camels and a pair of oxen. Ask ˹them˺, “Has He forbidden ˹to you˺ the two males or the two females or what is in the wombs of the two females? Or were you present when Allah gave you this commandment?”
phrases.explanation: Completing the eight mates of livestock with male and female camels and male and female cattle, the Prophet asks the same unanswerable question about whether Allah forbade the males, the females, or what is in their wombs, and then asks mockingly whether they were present as witnesses when Allah supposedly enjoined these taboos upon them.

phrases.translation: Who does more wrong than those who fabricate lies against Allah to mislead others without ˹any˺ knowledge? Surely Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people
phrases.explanation: No one is more unjust than someone who invents lies against Allah by attributing false prohibitions to Him in order to lead people astray out of ignorance, as the originators of pagan livestock taboos such as Amr ibn Luhayy did, and Allah does not guide wrongdoing people.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to eat except carrion, running blood, swine—which is impure—or a sinful offering in the name of any other than Allah.
phrases.explanation: Refuting the idolaters’ invented taboos over livestock and crops, the Prophet is commanded to declare that in the revelation sent down to him he finds nothing forbidden to an eater from what they prohibited, except carrion that died without slaughter, poured-out blood, the flesh of swine, which is impure, or a sinful offering slaughtered in a name other than Allah’s.

phrases.translation: But if someone is compelled by necessity—neither driven by desire nor exceeding immediate need—then surely your Lord is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
phrases.explanation: Even with those four forbidden meats, if someone is forced by starving necessity to eat of them in order to preserve life and ward off death, without craving what is unlawful out of indulgence or exceeding the amount needed to survive, the Lord is All-Forgiving and Most Merciful.

phrases.translation: For those who are Jewish, We forbade every animal with undivided hoofs and the fat of oxen and sheep except what is joined to their backs or intestines or mixed with bone.
phrases.explanation: Whereas the Arab idolaters falsely attributed their own taboos to Allah, Allah explains what He genuinely forbade earlier to the Jews: every animal and bird with undivided hoofs or claws, such as camels and ostriches, and the fat of cattle and sheep except what is attached to their backs or intestines or mixed with bone.

phrases.translation: In this way We rewarded them for their violations. And We are certainly truthful
phrases.explanation: Allah imposed those stricter dietary prohibitions of undivided hoofs and certain fats upon the Jews as a punishment and recompense for their own transgression and insolence against their Lord, and He is certainly truthful in reporting this against their claim that they merely followed what Jacob had forbidden to himself.

phrases.translation: But if they deny you ˹O Prophet˺, say, “Your Lord is infinite in mercy,
phrases.explanation: If the polytheists and deniers reject the message you have brought, tell them that your Lord possesses vast, all-encompassing mercy, by which He grants respite in this world and forgives whoever repents and turns back to Him. Vast divine mercy gives sinners every opportunity to repent before their term expires.

phrases.translation: yet His punishment will not be averted from the wicked people.”
phrases.explanation: At the same time warn them that when Allah’s decree arrives, His severe punishment can never be turned back from the wicked people who persist in disbelief and rebellion. Divine mercy never cancels divine justice against the unrepentant. Those who refuse Allah’s mercy until the end cannot escape His just punishment.

phrases.translation: The polytheists will argue, “Had it been Allah’s Will, neither we nor our forefathers would have associated others with Him ˹in worship˺ or made anything unlawful.” Likewise, those before them rejected the truth until they tasted Our punishment.
phrases.explanation: Cornered by clear proofs, the polytheists resort to a specious excuse, claiming that if Allah had disapproved of their idolatry and taboos He would have prevented them and their forefathers from practising them. Allah replies that earlier nations rejected their messengers with similar excuses until they tasted His punishment.

phrases.translation: Ask ˹them, O Prophet˺, “Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us? Surely you follow nothing but ˹false˺ assumptions and you do nothing but lie.”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is commanded to ask whether they possess any certain, revealed proof from Allah that He approves of their idolatry and livestock taboos so that they can bring it forth publicly. In truth they follow nothing but baseless conjecture and do nothing but fabricate lies against Allah.

phrases.translation: Say, “Allah has the most conclusive argument.
phrases.explanation: Refuting the polytheists’ claim that their idolatry was excused by divine decree, the Prophet is commanded to declare that to Allah alone belongs the conclusive, unanswerable proof against His servants after sending messengers and revealing Scriptures. By sending prophets and books, Allah has left humanity with no valid excuse for disobedience.

phrases.translation: Had it been His Will, He would have easily imposed guidance upon all of you.”
phrases.explanation: Had Allah willed to compel everyone to believe, He could easily have guided all humanity together to faith, yet He tests His servants through moral choice under clear command. Divine decree never serves as an excuse for disobeying divine command. Blaming divine decree for one’s own sins is a hollow pretext refuted by revelation.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Bring your witnesses who can testify that Allah has forbidden this.”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is commanded to challenge the polytheists who invented taboos over their crops and livestock to bring forward their witnesses who can testify that Allah actually forbade what they claim He forbade, thereby exposing before everyone that they possess no truthful witness for their fabrication.

phrases.translation: If they ˹falsely˺ testify, do not testify with them. And do not follow the desires of those who deny Our proofs, disbelieve in the Hereafter, and set up equals with their Lord
phrases.explanation: Even if they bring people who bear false witness to that lie, the Prophet and the believers must never endorse their testimony, nor follow the whims of those who deny Allah’s signs, disbelieve in the hereafter, and set up idols as equals to their Lord.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Come! Let me recite to you what your Lord has forbidden to you: do not associate others with Him ˹in worship˺. ˹Do not fail to˺ honour your parents.
phrases.explanation: Calling the people away from invented taboos to what Allah has truly decreed in revelation rather than conjecture, the Prophet invites them to hear what their Lord has forbidden and enjoined: never associate anything in creation as a partner with Allah in worship, and treat parents with dutiful kindness.

phrases.translation: Do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We provide for you and for them. Do not come near indecencies, openly or secretly.
phrases.explanation: People are forbidden to kill their children or bury their daughters alive out of fear of poverty and destitution, since Allah alone provides sustenance for both parents and children, and they are forbidden to approach shameful indecencies and major sins, whether committed openly or in secret.

phrases.translation: Do not take a ˹human˺ life—made sacred by Allah—except with ˹legal˺ right. This is what He has commanded you, so perhaps you will understand
phrases.explanation: Nor may anyone take a human life that Allah has made inviolable except by legal right, such as just retaliation for murder, capital punishment for married adultery, or apostasy from Islam. Allah has enjoined these commands so that people may use their reason and understand.

phrases.translation: And do not come near the wealth of the orphan—unless intending to enhance it—until they attain maturity. Give full measure and weigh with justice. We never require of any soul more than what it can afford.
phrases.explanation: Continuing the sacred commandments, Allah forbids approaching an orphan’s property except in the best manner, by preserving and investing it for the orphan’s benefit until they reach physical and mental maturity. People must also give full measure and weight with justice, while Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity if an unintentional shortfall occurs after honest effort.

phrases.translation: Whenever you speak, maintain justice—even regarding a close relative. And fulfil your covenant with Allah. This is what He has commanded you, so perhaps you will be mindful
phrases.explanation: Whenever believers speak in testimony, judgment, or statement, they must uphold truth and justice even if it goes against a close relative, and they must fulfil their covenant with Allah by obeying His commands. He has enjoined this so that they may be mindful and take heed.

phrases.translation: Indeed, that is My Path—perfectly straight. So follow it and do not follow other ways, for they will lead you away from His Way.
phrases.explanation: Pointing to the ten foundational commandments just recited, Allah declares that this religion of Islam is His straight path without crookedness, commanding believers to follow it alone and shun all divergent sects and innovations that scatter people away from His path. Unity upon Allah’s straight path protects believers from the scattering pull of sectarian desires.

phrases.translation: This is what He has commanded you, so perhaps you will be conscious ˹of Allah˺.”
phrases.explanation: Holding fast to the single straight path and avoiding sectarian division is what Allah has solemnly enjoined upon believers so that they may remain mindful of Him and safe from ruin. True mindfulness of Allah is preserved by clinging steadfastly to His uncrooked way rather than following scattered innovations.

phrases.translation: Additionally, We gave Moses the Scripture, completing the favour upon those who do good, detailing everything,
phrases.explanation: Furthermore, tell them that Allah gave Moses the Torah to complete His grace and favour upon the doers of good who obeyed His commands, and as a comprehensive explanation of all religious rulings they needed. The Torah stood as a complete favour and detailed law for the righteous of its era.

phrases.translation: and as a guide and a mercy, so perhaps they would be certain of the meeting with their Lord
phrases.explanation: The Torah was sent down as clear guidance and saving mercy for the Children of Israel so that they might believe with certainty in resurrection and the meeting with their Lord on Judgment Day. Every revealed Scripture prepares hearts to meet their Lord with certainty on Judgment Day.

phrases.translation: This is a blessed Book We have revealed.
phrases.explanation: Like the Scripture given to Moses before it, this Quran is a Book rich in blessing and enduring benefit that Allah has sent down to His final Messenger. Divine revelation is the greatest source of spiritual and moral blessing on earth. The Quran carries enduring blessing for everyone who recites, understands, and obeys it.

phrases.translation: So follow it and be mindful ˹of Allah˺, so you may be shown mercy
phrases.explanation: Humanity is therefore commanded to follow the Quran’s rulings and guard themselves against violating its sacred limits in reverent mindfulness of Allah, so that they may become worthy of His encompassing mercy. Following this blessed Book with an obedient heart is the surest road to divine compassion in both worlds.

phrases.translation: You ˹pagans˺ can no longer say, “Scriptures were only revealed to two groups before us
phrases.explanation: Allah revealed the Quran in clear Arabic so that the Arab polytheists could never excuse themselves on Judgment Day by claiming that heavenly Scriptures had been sent down only to the two communities before them, the Jews and the Christians. Revealing the Quran in Arabic removed any claim that Scripture belonged only to earlier nations.

phrases.translation: and we were unaware of their teachings.”
phrases.explanation: Nor can they plead that because those earlier books were in foreign tongues, they remained unaware of what those Scriptures studied and taught. With an Arabic Quran in their midst, every pretext of ignorance was removed. No listener who understands its clear message can plead ignorance on the Day of Reckoning.

phrases.translation: Nor can you say, “If only the Scriptures had been revealed to us, we would have been better guided than they.” Now there has come to you from your Lord a clear proof—a guide and mercy.
phrases.explanation: It also removes their boastful excuse that if a Book had been sent down to them in their own tongue, they would have been more rightly guided and obedient than the Jews and Christians. Now a clear proof, guidance, and mercy from their Lord has come to them through Muhammad and the Quran.

phrases.translation: Who then does more wrong than those who deny Allah’s revelations and turn away from them? We will reward those who turn away from Our revelations with a dreadful punishment for turning away
phrases.explanation: No one commits a greater wrong than someone who rejects Allah’s revelations and turns away from them after the excuse has been removed. Allah will repay those who turn away from His signs and hinder others from them with a dreadful punishment in hell for their aversion.

phrases.translation: Are they awaiting the coming of the angels, or your Lord ˹Himself˺, or some of your Lord’s ˹major˺ signs?
phrases.explanation: After rejecting every proof, are the idolaters waiting for the angels to arrive at death to take their souls, or for the Lord Himself to come on the Day of Resurrection, or for one of the Lord’s major signs, which prophetic reports identify as the sun rising from its western setting-place?

phrases.translation: On the Day your Lord’s signs arrive, belief will not benefit those who did not believe earlier or those who did no good through their faith. Say, “Keep waiting! We too are waiting.”
phrases.explanation: On the Day that unmistakable sign appears, newly professed faith will not benefit a disbeliever who did not believe beforehand, nor will faith benefit someone who earned no righteous deeds through it earlier. The Prophet is told to tell them to wait, for the believers too are waiting for Allah’s judgment.

phrases.translation: Indeed, you ˹O Prophet˺ are not responsible whatsoever for those who have divided their faith and split into sects.
phrases.explanation: Allah declares that the Prophet is completely clear of those who broke up the single true religion by accepting part of revelation and rejecting part, splitting into rival sects of Jews, Christians, and innovators. Splitting the single religion of Allah into rival sects is a betrayal of prophetic guidance.

phrases.translation: Their judgment rests only with Allah. And He will inform them of what they used to do
phrases.explanation: Their final affair and reckoning rest solely with Allah, and on the Day of Resurrection He will inform them of the divisions and innovations they used to commit and requite them accordingly. Allah alone will judge the sectarians and confront them with every division they created.

phrases.translation: Whoever comes with a good deed will be rewarded tenfold.
phrases.explanation: Proclaiming His boundless generosity on Judgment Day, Allah declares that whoever comes before Him as a believer bringing a single good deed will be rewarded with ten times its like in blessing and merit. Divine grace multiplies every sincere act of obedience. Multiplying every good deed tenfold shows how far Allah’s generosity exceeds strict accounting.

phrases.translation: But whoever comes with a bad deed will be punished for only one. None will be wronged
phrases.explanation: Conversely, whoever comes with an evil deed will be recompensed with only a single punishment equal to it without multiplication, and no soul will be wronged in the slightest by having its reward diminished or its burden unjustly increased. Punishing evil only one for one while multiplying good tenfold exemplifies divine justice and grace.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Surely my Lord has guided me to the Straight Path, a perfect way,
phrases.explanation: Summarizing the entire message of the surah, the Prophet is commanded to proclaim that his Lord has guided him to the straight path of Islam, an upright, uncrooked religion that establishes human affairs in truth. Islam is the straight, balanced religion that guides human life in harmony with truth.

phrases.translation: the faith of Abraham, the upright, who was not one of the polytheists.”
phrases.explanation: This straight path is the pure monotheistic creed of Abraham, who inclined wholly away from every false religion toward Allah alone and was never among the idolaters. Following the upright creed of Abraham means rejecting every trace of polytheism and dedicating worship exclusively to the Creator.

phrases.translation: Say, “Surely my prayer, my worship, my life, and my death are all for Allah—Lord of all worlds
phrases.explanation: Unlike the polytheists who prayed and slaughtered sacrifices for idols, the Prophet declares that his prayer, his sacrificial offerings and acts of devotion, the obedience he performs in life, and the faith upon which he dies belong purely to Allah, the Lord of all worlds.

phrases.translation: He has no partner. So I am commanded, and so I am the first to submit.”
phrases.explanation: Allah has no partner in any act of prayer, sacrifice, life, or death, and no created being shares in His divinity. With this exclusive devotion the Prophet was commanded by his Lord, and he is the first of his community to submit to Allah in Islam.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Should I seek a lord other than Allah while He is the Lord of everything?”
phrases.explanation: Responding to the idolaters who invited him to worship their graven images and follow Satan’s footsteps, the Prophet asks how he could ever seek a lord and master other than Allah when Allah alone is the sovereign Creator, Owner, Governor, and Sustainer of every existing thing.

phrases.translation: No one will reap except what they sow. No soul burdened with sin will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of your differences
phrases.explanation: Refuting the polytheists’ claim that they would carry the sins of anyone who followed their way, the verse affirms that every soul earns sin only against itself and no soul bears the burden of another. All will return to their Lord, who will judge and inform them regarding all the religious differences in which they disputed.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who has placed you as successors on earth and elevated some of you in rank over others, so He may test you with what He has given you.
phrases.explanation: Closing the surah, Allah reminds humanity that He made them successors on earth after bygone generations and raised some above others in ranks of wealth, strength, and worldly means so that He may test how they obey Him and fulfil His rights in what He has given them.

phrases.translation: Surely your Lord is swift in punishment, but He is certainly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: The Lord is swift in punishing those who rebel against His commands and fail the test of His worldly blessings, yet He is truly All-Forgiving in covering the faults of the repentant and Most Merciful toward those who turn back to Him in obedience before meeting Him.
